+      # THE BOT'S HALF OF THE DRIFT STEP (R11-PRE-SHARED-FILES part 1,
+      # countermeasure A of dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SELFTEST-SCOPE-DRIFT.md; the
+      # owner's ruling of 2026-11-18 on design decisions D1/D2, option (b)).
+      # Only where `drift` refused: `absorb` unions the table that step wrote
+      # into this head's committed table, each step whose run text is this
+      # head's, prints every read it adds, and the result is kept as the
+      # `selftest-absorbed` artifact. This job holds the workflow's read-only
+      # floor and no secret, so it commits nothing: no route with a write
+      # token commits tools/ci/selftest_closures.json (`closures-autofix`
+      # stages tests/closures.json on a pull request only; `record-autofix`
+      # stages delivery rows only, pinned by tests/entities.py), and the
+      # commit of that artifact is a seat's. A green push skips both steps
+      # and writes nothing. Red when `absorb` adds no read: a STALE,
+      # UNMEASURED or UNRECORDED step, which only `record` repairs.
+      - name: Absorb the drift step's measured reads into this head's table
+        id: absorb
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.drift.outcome == 'failure' }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/absorbed"
+          python3 -I tools/ci/selftest_scope.py absorb --from "$RUNNER_TEMP/selftest_closures.json" \
+            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/absorbed/selftest_closures.json" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/absorb.txt"
+          { echo '### selftest absorb'; echo '```'; cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/absorb.txt"; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
+          if ! grep -Eq '^selftest_scope absorb: [1-9][0-9]* read\(s\) added to [1-9][0-9]* step\(s\)$' "$RUNNER_TEMP/absorb.txt"; then
+            echo "selftest absorb: the drift step refused and absorb added no read; re-record the refused steps with selftest_scope.py record"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+      - name: Keep the absorbed table to commit
+        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.absorb.outcome == 'success' }}
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: selftest-absorbed
+          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/absorbed/selftest_closures.json
+          if-no-files-found: error
+
       # Last: a self-test started above whose status no step read would

+def _lower_bound_start(bounds: list[tuple[float, float]]) -> np.ndarray:
+    """The all-off start: every step at its lower bound (D0-s3-02).
+
+    Zero where a step is free, a forced-on pin's running floor where one
+    holds. Every other start buys energy, so without this one a day whose
+    optimum is to buy none -- negative prices on a storage plant, a house
+    the wood tank already carries -- is reached only if a descent finds it.
+    """
+    return np.array([low for low, _ in bounds], dtype=float)
+
+
+def _space_only_starts(
+    model: ThermalModel,
+    state: ThermalState,
+    target: float,
+    initial_power: np.ndarray,
+    reference_power: np.ndarray,
+    prices: np.ndarray,
+    bounds: list[tuple[float, float]],
+    p_max: float,
+    dt: float,
+) -> list[np.ndarray]:
+    """The space-only solve's multi-start set, the initial guess first.
+
+    The smooth price-weighted guess, a bang-bang schedule that buys the
+    cheapest steps first, the reference thermostat's own schedule, and the
+    low-energy bang-bang seeds (R1-D0-01 and R7-D0-01 -- see the two
+    fractions' comments for why the same-energy candidates all refine into
+    one basin on arbitrage prices, and why 0.35x alone does not bracket the
+    optimum's energy); the deep low-energy anchor is two-zone only, see its
+    own comment for why the reach is deliberately this narrow. See
+    ``_multi_start_minimize`` for why one guess is not enough.
+
+    The seeds scale with the share of the reference the wood tank covers,
+    so a tank covering it whole collapses them onto zero (D0-s2-01): the
+    price-ranked seeds are therefore also drawn at the reference's own
+    energy, and the all-off start brackets the set from below (D0-s3-02).
+    Byte-identical starts are kept once: with no wood cover the
+    reference-energy seeds are the scaled ones, and with whole cover the
+    scaled seeds and the all-off start are one zero schedule, each copy of
+    which would pay a full descent and polish to reach the same plan.
+    """
+    reference_kwh = float(np.sum(reference_power) * dt)
+    covered = _wood_covered_share(model, state, reference_kwh, target)
+    seed_power = reference_power * (1.0 - covered)
+    energy = float(np.sum(seed_power) * dt)
+    fractions = (_LOW_ENERGY_START_FRACTION,) + (
+        (_DEEP_LOW_ENERGY_START_FRACTION,) if model.params.two_zone_enabled else ()
+    )
+    starts = [
+        initial_power,
+        _price_ranked_start(prices, energy, p_max, dt),
+        seed_power,  # inside the bounds: the reference never passes the pump
+        *(_price_ranked_start(prices, energy * f, p_max, dt) for f in fractions),
+    ]
+    starts.extend(
+        _price_ranked_start(prices, reference_kwh * f, p_max, dt)
+        for f in (1.0, *fractions)
+    )
+    starts.append(_lower_bound_start(bounds))
+    unique: dict[bytes, np.ndarray] = {}
+    for start in starts:
+        unique.setdefault(np.asarray(start, dtype=float).tobytes(), start)
+    return list(unique.values())
+
+

+# D3-s1, box D3-m5: D3.M5 resource use (round 11, resume slice)
+
+Baseline `92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692`. box D3-m5: Linux 6.18 x86_64, nproc 4, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, 16 GB, venv-ci CPython 3.14.7 (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1), node v22.23.5, alone on the box. Every wall/CPU/RSS figure is
+**provisional** (the judge re-takes it); counts are final. D3-s1-01 (env_drift's capture
+child drops the reach hook) is already judged and is cited here, not re-reported.
+
+## Method
+
+R0 restored the carried evidence from `c0adbc19` (no box checkpoint existed). R1 re-took
+every driver's traced baseline on this box (21/21 green), re-traced env_drift's capture
+child, and re-ran both controls: null LIVES over 16 drivers, positive 2/2 KILLED by
+`tests/manual_plan.py`. Then D3.M5 (a) to (e), with nothing else running during (a).
+
+Universe: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/enumerate.py --scripts`, 27 closure scripts reaching the cells; all 27 examined.
+Redispatched C1, C4, C7, C9: examined.
+
+## Rows carried for D3.M1 to D3.M4
+
+M1 1260/1260 and M4 35/35 as carried. M2 34/1260 as carried; the remainder is assigned to boxes D3-u1a, D3-u1b, D3-u1c, D3-u1d. M3: this box's matrix is the full net on all 35 survivors (19 killed, 16 survive); C3, the top-six full gate, is assigned to box D3-top6.
+
+Full net, no early stop, every closure script of the file (27 incl. stress alone, golden strict, card scripts behind plan_view), on all 35 survivors: it is box D3-m5's M5(b) kill matrix, whose mutant set contains every SURVIVED verdict under results/{pre,c2,c3c6} (PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_matrix.py table -v; drives under state/results/matrix and matrix-stress, D3S1_RELAX=0). 19 of 35 killed (features.py 18 of them; harness_headers.py alone kills thermal_model.py:270, by SIGXCPU in an audit harness, features.py timing out on it), 16 survive every script: coordinator.py:8806 M04, dhw_planner.py:1559 M19, flow_lift.py:47 CONST, :183 GUARD_OFF, :188 M35, grid_fee.py:173 GUARD_OFF, :355 M36, :383 M21, optimizer.py:773 GUARD_OFF, price_model.py:252 M34, :337 M25, sysid.py:610 GUARD_OFF, tariff.py:744 M31, thermal_model.py:169 GUARD_OFF, :835 M03, :2593 M07. Of the carried top six, tariff.py:64, price_model.py:201, coordinator.py:539, sysid.py:2246 M27 and sysid.py:1549 M26 are KILLED by tests/features.py; tariff.py:744 M31 survives. C3, the GATE_SCOPE=full GOLDEN_MODE=drift gate for the top six, is not driven here (assigned to box D3-top6). C5 answered by the carried run's REPORT.md. Counts exact; seconds provisional.

+
+## Findings
+
+### D3-s1-52 (low, hygiene): card_drift.mjs inherits plan_view.py closure, yet compares two cards over one payload: no cell edit can move it
+
+tests/closure.py's _widen unions tests/plan_view.py's closure into tests/card_drift.mjs's, so 11 of the 12 D3-s1 cell files schedule card_drift on every one-file diff (closure.select), yet card_drift renders the working tree's card and the ref's card against ONE shared plan payload, so a production edit that changes that payload (sha256 differs) leaves 0 of its 45 states moved, while a one-token card edit moves 44.
+
+Mechanism: PRODUCERS = {'tests/card.mjs': [plan_view], 'tests/card_drift.mjs': [plan_view]} is used twice: as a selection-ordering edge (a selected card script needs its producer first: sound) and, in _widen, as a closure union ('anything that can change the payload can change what they test'). The union is sound for card.mjs, whose checks are absolute assertions over the payload, and unsound for card_drift.mjs, whose verdict is byte-equality of two card renders that both read the same payload in one process (tests/card_drift.mjs header, renderAll over makeSide(treeSrc) and makeSide(baseSrc)). A cell-file diff changes only the payload, which both sides share, and touches neither the card source nor a solver fixture (claimsAreThisBranchs), so the comparison is an identity.
+
+Evidence: `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py`: base moved 0/45; prod_small and prod_large
+(payload sha256 changed) moved 0/45; card arm moved 44/45 (rc 0 -> 1).
+`--select-only`: 11 of 12 single-cell-file diffs schedule card_drift.mjs. Matrix: card_drift
+0 kills of 10 driven. Cost 4.0 s wall per cell diff (provisional). Fix scope:
+tests/closure.py: keep card_drift.mjs's PRODUCERS entry for selection ORDER (a card diff still runs plan_view first) but stop _widen from unioning the producer's closure into card_drift.mjs's; re-derive its closures.json entry (its raw trace was 6 files, #527). Verify with this harness's --select-only (11 -> 0) and the card arm (still 44).
+
+## Non-findings
+
+- boost_drift_replay.py's and stress.py's measured closures do not over-approximate for the cell files: every cell file in each closure is executed by the traced run. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_trace_hastub.py --scripts tests/stress.py,tests/boost_drift_replay.py` -> boost_drift_replay 12/12 files executed (5849 lines), stress 6/6 (5189 lines); over_approx_pairs=0; m5_closure_reach.py: 0 of 245 pairs over 22 traced drivers
+- closures.json recorded.seconds stays inside closure.py's 2x SECONDS_BAND for 22 of the 27 cell-closure scripts on a quiet box; the two differential guards record their documented stub (#934) and mutation_table keeps env_drift eager for that reason. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_gate_table.py` -> in band 22/27; out: env_drift 96.4x, golden 80.8x (stubs), harness_headers 0.44x, plan_view 0.44x, wood_advisor 0.43x (all provisional, load1 0.7-1.1)
+- boost_drift_replay.py's low checks-per-solve (46/789) is not unasserted work: its solves drive the 9-day closed-loop replay whose learner trajectory the checks read. `cat dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/solves.jsonl; sed -n 1,40p tests/boost_drift_replay.py` -> 0.058 checks per solve; 3 arms x 9 days of 30-minute cycles, each cycle's solve adopted and actuated (header); no perturbation showing a check independent of the solves was found
+- stress.py and env_drift.py assert at a density of the same order as the other solve-heavy scripts. `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_solves.py --hastub-hook --scripts tests/stress.py,tests/env_drift.py` -> stress 0.48, env_drift 1.12 cold / 2.24 warm checks per solve, against edge 0.95, backtest 2.27, optimality 3.65
+- harness_headers.py's matrix kills are behavioural, not contention artefacts of its CPU bounds. `python3 -c "import json,glob;[print(k,j['checks'][:2]) for f in glob.glob('dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/results/matrix/*.json') for k,j in json.load(open(f))['runs'].items() if k=='tests/harness_headers.py' and j['killed']]"` -> 4 kills: 3 are RESULT-header mismatches of audit harnesses driving production (sysid_estimator_frontier, dst_window_factors); 1 (thermal_model.py:270) a SIGXCPU at the 480 CPU-s bound that features.py also timed out on (2314 s)
+- golden.py's closure edges cost the CI gate nothing: CI runs GOLDEN_MODE=drift, which skips golden.py; its strict mode (run.sh's local default) is red at baseline on a non-canonical machine and can kill no cell mutant here. `grep -rn GOLDEN_MODE .github/workflows/; PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_matrix.py table | grep golden` -> tests.yml:374 and nightly.yml:496 set drift; strict baseline 55 of 56 changed; 0 of 38 mutants killed
+- The mutation-lane cost D3-s1-01 names shows in the no-early-stop matrix: env_drift kills nothing on lines its capture never executes (cited, not re-reported). `matrix rows of dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/results/matrix/ against baselines.json capture_reach (see REPORT.md, (b))` -> 21 of 38 matrix mutants on lines the capture never executes; env_drift killed 0 of those 21 (2 of the other 17)
+- Pre-screen instrument controls hold on this box. `cat dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/m5box-null.out dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/m5box-posctl.out` -> null LIVES over 16 drivers; positive 2/2 KILLED by tests/manual_plan.py
+
+## Leads (outside the cells)
+
+- D3-s3 `tests/gate_lock.py` `needs_lease / _recorded_seconds`: Classifies a SCOPE_RUN as light ('none', unleased) when every name's closures.json recorded.seconds is under SLOT_MIN_SECONDS=69, but tests/env_drift.py (1.0 s) and tests/golden.py (1.2 s) record a stub invocation (#934) while a real run measured 96-197 s and 97 s here (m5_gate_table.py); a scope that selects only those two plus light scripts would run unleased.
+- D3-s3 `tests/card_drift.mjs` `the closing process.exit(1) after console.log`: Exiting with process.exit right after console.log truncates a PIPED stdout: captured through subprocess capture_output, a card edit's run showed 1 of 44 DRIFT lines and no summary, a file redirect all 44 (measured while building m5_card_drift_payload.py). Any instrument reading card_drift's (or card.mjs's) verdict through a pipe reads a truncated count.

+   "value": "85.6 s and 88.7 s measured; tests/closure.py CLOSURES_COMMENT (#934) states the record times the key print; mutation_table REF_DRIVEN keeps env_drift eager for that reason"
+  },
+  {
+   "claim": "The fast pre-screen net's survivors overstate the suite's gaps: the full net kills most of them",
+   "command": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_matrix.py table",
+   "value": "19 of 35 fast-net survivors killed by the full net, 18 by features.py; a pre-screen survivor is a candidate only (D3.md step 3), and the gate's scoped run always includes features.py for these files"
+  },
+  {
+   "claim": "The pre-screen harness can kill on this box (positive control) and lives on the unmutated tree (null)",
+   "command": "cat dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/m5-posctl.out dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/state/m5-null.out",
+   "value": "2/2 KILLED by tests/manual_plan.py; null LIVES over 18 drivers"
+  }
+ ],
+ "leads": [
+  {
+   "owner_seat": "unknown",
+   "file": "tests/gate_lock.py",
+   "symbol": "needs_lease / _recorded_seconds",
+   "what": "needs_lease reads closures.json recorded.seconds (env_drift.py 1.0 s, the --cache-key stub) against SLOT_MIN_SECONDS=69, so env_drift.py --all, measured 85.6 s here, is classed 'none' (unleased) in a scoped gate; D11 universe, not measured by this seat"
+  }
+ ],
+ "md_head": "# D3-s1 round 11, box D3-m5 report (baseline 92d38ecb)\n\nThis box's slice: D3.M5 (a)-(e) on a quiet box. Seat run inline in the box session (orchestrator inbox 1: no Agent spawn). Carried evidence restored from box D3R's return (c0adbc19); rows D3.M1-M4 are carried as D3R left them, their remainder assigned to boxes D3-top6 and D3-u1a..d. D3-s1-01 is cited, not re-reported. box D3-m5: Linux x86_64, nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.30GHz, 16 GB, alone on the box (load1 0.05-1.3 during timed measures, 4.0 during the 4-worker matrix); every wall/CPU number provisional, counts final.\n\n## Method\n\nR1: traced baselines of 24 drivers re-taken on this box, null and positive controls re-run. (a) m5_gate_table.py runs each of the 27 closure scripts alone as run.sh invokes it. (b) prescreen.py run --full --sub matrix with relaxation off over 38 mutants (m5_matrix.py builds the sample and tables it). (c) m5_solves.py, now running env_drift's capture child under the hook. (d)/(e) m5_trace_extra.py traces card.mjs, card_drift.mjs, golden.py, stress.py (and plan_view.py as the Node programs' producer) and tests each closure edge against executed lines.",
+ "harnesses_add": [
+  "m5_gate_table.py",
+  "m5_matrix.py",
+  "m5_trace_extra.py",
+  "m5_box_report.py"
+ ],
+ "exposure_add": "Box D3-m5 run (inline in the box session): read COMMON.md, D3.md, dev/audit/README.md (harness contract), finding.schema.json and tests/mutation_table.py, tests/run.sh, tests/closures.json, tests/closure.py and tests/gate_lock.py excerpts (through haiku extractors/scout), the carried harnesses, REPORT.json and LOCAL-REPORT.json; no docs/ or GitHub read beyond the box's dispatch/inbox/wip refs."
+}

diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..b4f45bcb6d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report.py
@@ -0,0 +1,133 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""D3-s1: assemble REPORT.json's coverage rows from the seat's state.
+
+Metric (one line): per step, universe = lines its enumerator prints at the
+baseline, examined = items the step's method ran on (state/results), and
+not_reached = the rest, grouped by file past the schema's 200-item cap.
+Run: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report.py
+Reads state/ and the hand-written findings.json/non_findings.json/leads.json
+beside it; writes REPORT.json. Counts are exact; no timing claims.
+Instrumented symbol: tests/mutation_table.py:inventory/unpinned_sites (via
+enumerate.py). Perturbation: removing a results file lowers `examined` by one
+and adds its site to not_reached.
+Baseline: 92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692. Machine: owner macOS arm64.
+"""
+import os
+for _v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
+           "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS", "VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS"):
+    os.environ.setdefault(_v, "1")
+import json
+import sys
+from collections import defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE))
+sys.argv = sys.argv[:1]
+import prescreen as p  # noqa: E402
+
+REL = "dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1"
+BASE = "92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692"
+
+
+def load(sub):
+    d = p.RESULTS / sub
+    return {q.stem: json.loads(q.read_text()) for q in d.glob("*.json")} if d.exists() else {}
+
+
+def site_id(m):
+    return f"{m['file']}:{m['line']} {m['kind']} {m['anchor'].split()[-1]}"
+
+
+def grouped(items, cap=200):
+    if len(items) <= cap:
+        return [site_id(m) for m in items]
+    by = defaultdict(list)
+    for m in items:
+        by[m["file"]].append(m["line"])
+    return [f"{f}: {len(ls)} unpinned sites not pre-screened (lines {min(ls)}-{max(ls)})"
+            for f, ls in sorted(by.items())]
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    uni = p.unpinned()
+    keys = {p.key(m): m for m in uni}
+    pre, c2, c36, comp = load("pre"), load("c2"), load("c3c6"), load("complete")
+    # inventory sites the R10 re-drawn mutants coincide with count as examined
+    by_site = {(m["file"], m["line"], m["new"]): p.key(m) for m in uni}
+    examined = set(k for k in pre if k in keys)
+    for r in list(c2.values()) + list(c36.values()):
+        m = r["mutant"]
+        k = by_site.get((m["file"], m["line"], m["new"]))
+        if k:
+            examined.add(k)
+    m2_nr = [m for k, m in keys.items() if k not in examined]
+    surv = {k: r for sub in (pre, c2, c36) for k, r in sub.items()
+            if r["verdict"] == "SURVIVED"}
+    m3_done = [k for k in surv if k in comp]
+    m3_nr = [surv[k]["mutant"] for k in surv if k not in comp]
+    scripts = [ln.split("\t")[0] for ln in
+               os.popen(f"PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 {REL}/enumerate.py --scripts").read().splitlines()]
+    base = json.loads((p.STATE / "baselines.json").read_text())
+    solved = {json.loads(ln)["script"] for ln in
+              (p.STATE / "solves.jsonl").read_text().splitlines() if ln.strip()}
+    m5_ex = [s for s in scripts if s in base or s in solved]
+    m5_nr = [s for s in scripts if s not in m5_ex]
+    extra = json.loads((HERE / "report_extra.json").read_text())
+    cov = [
+        {"step": "D3.M1",
+         "enumerator": f"PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 {REL}/enumerate.py --unpinned",
+         "universe": len(uni), "examined": len(uni), "not_reached": [],
+         "redispatched": extra["redispatched"]["D3.M1"],
+         "evidence": extra["evidence"]["D3.M1"]},
+        {"step": "D3.M2",
+         "enumerator": f"PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 {REL}/enumerate.py --unpinned",
+         "universe": len(uni), "examined": len(examined),
+         "not_reached": grouped(m2_nr),
+         "redispatched": extra["redispatched"]["D3.M2"],
+         "evidence": extra["evidence"]["D3.M2"]},
+        {"step": "D3.M3",
+         "enumerator": f"PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 {REL}/tabulate.py --tsv | grep -P '\\tSURVIVED\\t'",
+         "universe": len(surv), "examined": len(m3_done),
+         "not_reached": [site_id(m) for m in m3_nr],
+         "redispatched": extra["redispatched"]["D3.M3"],
+         "evidence": extra["evidence"]["D3.M3"]},
+        {"step": "D3.M4",
+         "enumerator": f"PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 {REL}/tabulate.py --tsv | grep -P '\\tSURVIVED\\t'",
+         "universe": len(surv), "examined": len(extra["m4_answered"]),
+         "not_reached": [site_id(surv[k]["mutant"]) for k in surv
+                         if k not in extra["m4_answered"]],
+         "redispatched": extra["redispatched"]["D3.M4"],
+         "evidence": extra["evidence"]["D3.M4"]},
+        {"step": "D3.M5",
+         "enumerator": f"PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 {REL}/enumerate.py --scripts",
+         "universe": len(scripts), "examined": len(m5_ex), "not_reached": m5_nr,
+         "redispatched": extra["redispatched"]["D3.M5"],
+         "evidence": extra["evidence"]["D3.M5"]},
+    ]
+    for row in cov:
+        assert row["examined"] + (len(row["not_reached"]) if len(row["not_reached"]) <= 200 and not any(": " in x and "not pre-screened" in x for x in row["not_reached"]) else row["universe"] - row["examined"]) == row["universe"], row["step"]
+    rep = {
+        "dimension": "D3", "baseline_sha": BASE,
+        "report_path": f"{REL}/REPORT.md",
+        "exposure": extra["exposure"],
+        "coverage": cov,
+        "unfinished": extra["unfinished"],
+        "findings": json.loads((HERE / "findings.json").read_text()),
+        "non_findings": extra["non_findings"],
+        "harnesses": [f"{REL}/{n}" for n in (
+            "enumerate.py", "prescreen.py", "tabulate.py", "m5_closure_reach.py",
+            "m5_solves.py", "m5_envdrift_reach.py", "build_report.py", "finalize.py")],
+        "leads": extra["leads"],
+    }
+    (HERE / "REPORT.json").write_text(json.dumps(rep, indent=1) + "\n")
+    for row in cov:
+        print(f"RESULT {row['step']}_universe={row['universe']} examined={row['examined']} not_reached_items={len(row['not_reached'])}")
+    print(f"RESULT survivors={len(surv)} completed={len(m3_done)}")
+    print("RESULT thread_factor=1.00")
+    print(f"RESULT load1={os.getloadavg()[0]:.2f}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report_rem.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report_rem.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..696d0c4d3d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report_rem.py
@@ -0,0 +1,201 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+# Box D3-rem report assembly for seat D3-s1 (round 11, D3.M3 remainder and its D3.M4 answers).
+# Command: python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/build_report_rem.py
+# Reads: t2_results.json (probe verdicts, each re-run by the box seat), state/gates/<key>.json
+# (fullgate.py verdicts), REPORT.json as carried from box D3-top6 (kept as REPORT-D3-top6.json).
+# Writes: REPORT-D3-rem.json, REPORT-D3-rem.md, findings/<id>.json. Counts are exact; walls are provisional.
+import json
+import os
+import shutil
+
+HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
+REL = "dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1"
+BASE = "92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692"
+MACHINE = "box D3-rem: Linux x86_64, nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, 16 GB, venv-ci CPython 3.14, alone on the box"
+
+
+def j(p):
+    with open(os.path.join(HERE, p)) as f:
+        return json.load(f)
+
+
+carried_path = os.path.join(HERE, "REPORT-D3-top6.json")
+if not os.path.exists(carried_path):
+    shutil.copy(os.path.join(HERE, "REPORT.json"), carried_path)
+carried = j("REPORT-D3-top6.json")
+T2 = j("t2_results.json")
+
+
+def gate(key):
+    p = os.path.join(HERE, "state/gates", key + ".json")
+    return json.load(open(p)) if os.path.exists(p) else None
+
+
+T1 = [("c2", "95779f9d6d71c50d", "grid_fee.py:355"), ("c2", "a0b3b28854fa500c", "flow_lift.py:188"),
+      ("c2", "c38d53ab787ddbfa", "price_model.py:252"), ("c3c6", "5cc84148fa68bda1", "grid_fee.py:383"),
+      ("c3c6", "a4b00ac3ca662eec", "thermal_model.py:835")]
+CARRIED_T1 = {"95779f9d6d71c50d", "a0b3b28854fa500c"}
+
+
+def t1_row(src, key, site):
+    g = gate(key) or {}
+    v = g.get("verdict") or ("SURVIVED" if g.get("gate_rc") == 0 else "?")
+    survived = v in ("SURVIVED", "RED-AS-NULL")
+    ld = "%s..%s" % (g.get("load1_start", "-"), g.get("load1_end", "-"))
+    how = "carried from cloud box D3-top6 (wip 917689bd)" if key in CARRIED_T1 else "gated on box D3-rem"
+    return dict(mutant="%s:%s" % (src, key), site=site, verdict=v, survived=survived,
+                killed_by=g.get("killed_by") or [], wall_s=g.get("wall_s"), load1=ld, carried_or_gated=how)
+
+
+t1 = [t1_row(*r) for r in T1]
+
+# Findings: survivors whose probe metric moves on an input production admits.
+SPEC = [
+    ("121362d48b408236", "grid_fee:_parse_rule", "No check feeds a grid-fee rule without '=' to _parse_rule; dropping the guard is unseen",
+     "rules_mutant", 1, "accepted rule count for rules text '0.5' (baseline -1 = GridFeeError)", "up",
+     "A grid-fee rule line with no '= rate' part is refused with GridFeeError (spec_problem reports invalid_grid_fee_rules)"),
+    ("95779f9d6d71c50d", "grid_fee:GridFeeSchedule.max_abs_component", "No check pins max_abs_component's source label on a fixed/rule |rate| tie",
+     "label_changed", 1, "1 when the (value, source) label of max_abs_component differs from baseline on the fixed=0.25 / rule=0.25 tie", "up",
+     "On a tie between the fixed fee and a rule, max_abs_component keeps the first-seen (fixed) source"),
+    ("5cc84148fa68bda1", "grid_fee:GridFeeSchedule.min_component", "No check pins min_component's source label on a fixed/rule rate tie",
+     "label_changed", 1, "1 when the (value, source) label of min_component differs from baseline on the fixed=-0.25 / rule=-0.25 tie", "up",
+     "On a tie between the fixed fee and a rule, min_component keeps the first-seen (fixed) source"),
+    ("0c3e91a6a349409a", "flow_lift:FLOW_BIAS_ALPHA (read in FlowCurveBias.observe)", "No check pins FLOW_BIAS_ALPHA's value; doubling the flow-bias EWMA weight is unseen",
+     "delta", 1.05124, "learned flow bias in K after 5 residuals of +2 K then 5 of +6 K", "up",
+     "The flow-bias EWMA after warm-up weights each new residual by exactly the documented 0.1"),
+    ("a0b3b28854fa500c", "flow_lift:FlowCurveBias.observe", "No check folds the sample one past FLOW_BIAS_MIN_SAMPLES; the warm-up boundary is unpinned",
+     "delta", 0.666667, "learned flow bias in K after five +2 K residuals then a +12 K sixth", "up",
+     "The sample at samples == FLOW_BIAS_MIN_SAMPLES is folded as an EWMA, not as part of the warm-up mean"),
+    ("050fdc4a20eba212", "thermal_model:_holiday_dhw_windows", "No check pins that an unset holiday-DHW-windows option parses to None, not []",
+     "unset_forms_moved", 3, "count of unset option forms (absent, '', None) whose parsed holiday windows differ from baseline None", "up",
+     "An unset holiday DHW windows option leaves the ordinary windows in force on holidays (parses to None)"),
+    ("22b5ec8775d5bd50", "thermal_model:_valve_two_zone_delivery", "No check bounds single-tank valve delivery by the tank energy over dt; max->min is unseen",
+     "delta", 2.5216, "valve-delivered heat in kW from a 20 L tank at 24 C, manual valve target 35 C, dt 0.25 h", "up",
+     "Heat a valve draws from a single tank in one step never exceeds the tank's usable energy divided by dt"),
+    ("0911281eca895664", "dhw_planner:DhwPlanner._plan_dhw_min_cost", "No check makes the DHW shortfall penalty bind; its max->min price base is unseen",
+     "delta_kwh", -0.5108, "planned DHW kWh over 12 steps (60 C floor), steps 0-10 at 100000, step 11 at 0", "down",
+     "The DHW shortfall price exceeds every step's price so meeting the floor always wins"),
+    ("5e8d48eff7e4fa8d", "coordinator:HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._on_power_event", "No check covers _on_power_event with the tariff disabled or its factor 0; and->or is unseen",
+     "caseA_threshold_mutant", 3.0, "guard threshold kW (baseline 10.0 = fuse) with tariff disabled and a 3 kW restored tracker peak", "down",
+     "The peak-tariff threshold caps the power guard only when the tariff is enabled and its factor is positive"),
+    ("c38d53ab787ddbfa", "price_model:PriceShapeModel.observe_day_quarters", "No check feeds observe_day_quarters a day whose mean is exactly 1e-6",
+     "accepted_mutant", 1, "quarter-days accepted for a day of 48x0.0 and 48x2e-6 (mean exactly 1e-6; baseline 0)", "up",
+     "A price day with mean <= 1e-6 is rejected by the quarter-shape learner"),
+]
+
+
+def finding(n, spec):
+    key, sym, title, rname, val, metric, direction, prop = spec
+    r = T2[key]
+    g = gate(key) or {}
+    probe = r["probe"]
+    path = probe.split("python3 ")[1].split()[0]
+    fid = "D3-s1-%02d" % n
+    return {
+        "id": fid, "scope": "D3-s1", "step": "D3.M3", "title": title[:120], "severity": "low",
+        "claim": "Mutant %s at %s survives the full gate (%s), yet the probe's %s moves: baseline %s, mutant %s." % (
+            key, r["site"], g.get("verdict", "?"), rname, r["baseline"], r["mutant"]),
+        "mechanism": "Reach: %s. Check that should have failed (D3.M4): %s." % (r["reach"], r["should_fail"]),
+        "evidence": {"command": probe, "harness_path": path, "value": val, "unit": metric,
+                     "baseline_sha": BASE, "machine": MACHINE, "cpu_or_wall": "n/a",
+                     "contention_note": "deterministic value; probes ran while box D3-rem gates ran (load1 ~1); the full-gate walls in the T1 table are provisional",
+                     "tolerance": "exact", "load1": 1.0, "thread_factor": 1.0},
+        "instrumented_symbol": "custom_components.heatpump_optimizer." + sym,
+        "perturbation": {"change": "the mutant edit at %s applied in memory by the probe (%s); full gate: fullgate.py run --key %s" % (r["site"], r["input"], key),
+                         "expected_direction": direction, "observed_value": val},
+        "metric_definition": metric[:200],
+        "phenomenon_property": prop,
+        "seam_rule": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 %s/tabulate.py --tsv | grep -P '\\tSURVIVED\\t'" % REL,
+        "null_control": {"command": probe, "value": r["null_delta"], "note": "null arm where the edit cannot matter; identical floats under both arms"},
+        "reproduction_steps": [probe, "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 %s/fullgate.py run --src %s --key %s" % (REL, r["src"], key)],
+        "proposed_fix_scope": "tests only: a check at the boundary input above that pins the baseline value (%s)" % r["baseline"],
+        "files": ["custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/" + r["site"].split(":")[0], "tests/features.py"],
+        "stop_rule_class": "hygiene", "class_guess": "new",
+    }
+
+
+def main():
+    survived = {r["mutant"].split(":")[1] for r in t1 if r["survived"]}
+    findings = []
+    n = 62
+    for spec in SPEC:
+        key = spec[0]
+        if key in [x[1] for x in T1] and key not in survived:
+            continue
+        if T2.get(key, {}).get("verdict", "").startswith("finding"):
+            findings.append(finding(n, spec))
+            n += 1
+    os.makedirs(os.path.join(HERE, "findings"), exist_ok=True)
+    for f in findings:
+        json.dump(f, open(os.path.join(HERE, "findings", f["id"] + ".json"), "w"), indent=1)
+
+    nf = []
+    for r in t1:
+        nf.append({"claim": "T1 full gate %s %s: %s (%s)" % (r["mutant"], r["site"], r["verdict"], r["carried_or_gated"]),
+                   "command": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 %s/fullgate.py run --src %s --key %s" % (REL, *r["mutant"].split(":")),
+                   "value": "killed_by=%s; wall %s s, load1 %s (provisional)" % (r["killed_by"] or "none", r["wall_s"], r["load1"])})
+    nf.append({"claim": "box D3-rem full-gate null control: red only on artefact checks no production mutant can need (state/gates/null-D3-rem-note.txt)",
+               "command": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 %s/fullgate.py null" % REL,
+               "value": "gate_rc=1; closure.py selftest 2, entities.py 1 of 2723, harness_headers.py 4 failing lines; wall 3215.1 s, load1 1.55..1.0 (provisional)"})
+    for key, r in T2.items():
+        if r["verdict"].startswith("non-finding"):
+            if key == "a4b00ac3ca662eec" and key not in survived:
+                continue
+            nf.append({"claim": "T2 %s %s: %s; reach: %s" % (key, r["site"], r["verdict"], r["reach"]),
+                       "command": r["probe"], "value": "baseline %s; mutant %s; null delta %s" % (r["baseline"], r["mutant"], r["null_delta"])})
+
+    cov = []
+    for row in carried["coverage"]:
+        row = dict(row)
+        if row["step"] == "D3.M3":
+            row["examined"] = row["universe"]
+            row["not_reached"] = []
+            row["evidence"] = ("box D3-top6 gated 30 of 35 (carried, state/gates/ and state/gates/cloud/); box D3-rem gated the "
+                               "remaining 5 (2 carried from cloud box D3-top6 wip 917689bd, 3 gated here: state/gates/c38d53ab787ddbfa.json, "
+                               "5cc84148fa68bda1.json, a4b00ac3ca662eec.json) and probed every full-gate survivor without a finding "
+                               "(t2_results.json, probe_*.py). T1 table: " + json.dumps(t1))
+        elif row["step"] == "D3.M4":
+            row["evidence"] = row["evidence"] + " | box D3-rem: each survivor's answer re-derived by a moving probe (t2_results.json: production line, file, the check that should have failed)."
+        else:
+            row["evidence"] = "assigned to boxes D3-u1a..d / D3-m5 (carried unchanged from box D3-top6's return). " + row["evidence"]
+        cov.append(row)
+
+    harnesses = sorted({"%s/%s" % (REL, p) for p in os.listdir(HERE) if p.startswith("probe_") and p.endswith(".py")}
+                       | {REL + "/fullgate.py", REL + "/build_report_rem.py"})
+    rep = {
+        "dimension": "D3", "baseline_sha": BASE, "report_path": REL + "/REPORT-D3-rem.md",
+        "exposure": carried.get("exposure", "") + " Box D3-rem read box D3-top6's carried REPORT.md and REPORT.json (fdd9e2d8) and two gate results from its wip tree (917689bd); no GitHub reads.",
+        "coverage": cov, "unfinished": [], "findings": findings, "non_findings": nf,
+        "harnesses": harnesses, "leads": [],
+    }
+    md = ["# D3-s1, box D3-rem: D3.M3 remainder and its D3.M4 answers", "",
+          "Baseline %s. %s. Walls provisional; counts exact." % (BASE, MACHINE), "",
+          "## T1 full gate", "", "| mutant | site | survived | killed_by | wall s | load1 | carried-or-gated |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
+    for r in t1:
+        md.append("| %s | %s | %s (%s) | %s | %s | %s | %s |" % (r["mutant"], r["site"], r["survived"], r["verdict"],
+                  ",".join(r["killed_by"]) or "-", r["wall_s"], r["load1"], r["carried_or_gated"]))
+    md += ["", "Null control on this box: gate_rc=1 on artefact checks only (state/gates/null-D3-rem-note.txt); RED-AS-NULL = no script fails more checks than the null.", "",
+           "## T2 probes", "", "| mutant | site | probe command | baseline value | mutant value | null delta | finding-or-non-finding |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
+    fid = {f["reproduction_steps"][1].split("--key ")[1]: f["id"] for f in findings}
+    for key, r in T2.items():
+        if key in [x[1] for x in T1] and key not in survived:
+            continue
+        verdict = fid.get(key, r["verdict"])
+        md.append("| %s | %s | `%s` | %s | %s | %s | %s |" % (key, r["site"], r["probe"], r["baseline"], r["mutant"], r["null_delta"], verdict))
+    md += ["", "## D3.M4 answers (production line, file, the check that should have failed)", ""]
+    for key, r in T2.items():
+        md.append("- %s %s: %s. Should have failed: %s" % (key, r["site"], r["symbol"], r["should_fail"]))
+    md += ["", "## Findings", ""] + ["- %s: %s" % (f["id"], f["title"]) for f in findings]
+    rep["report_md"] = "\n".join(md) + "\n"
+    try:
+        open(os.path.join(HERE, "REPORT-D3-rem.md"), "w").write(rep["report_md"])
+    except OSError as e:
+        rep["unfinished"].append({"step": "D3.M3", "what": "REPORT.md write refused (%s); its content is in report_md" % e})
+    json.dump(rep, open(os.path.join(HERE, "REPORT-D3-rem.json"), "w"), indent=1)
+    print("RESULT findings=%d count" % len(findings))
+    print("RESULT non_findings=%d count" % len(nf))
+    print("RESULT t1_survived=%d of %d" % (len(survived), len(t1)))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/enumerate.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/enumerate.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..6941384b81
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/enumerate.py
@@ -0,0 +1,74 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""D3-s1 enumerator: the step universe for D3.M1-M5 over the seat's cells.
+
+Metric: every candidate site tests/mutation_table.py's ratcheted inventory
+generates in the 12 cell files, with its disposition (unpinned / killed_by /
+triaged), one line per site: `<file>:<line>\t<kind>\t<anchor>\t<disposition>`.
+The universe of M1/M2/M3/M4 is the UNPINNED lines (`--unpinned`); M5's is the
+closure scripts reaching the cell files (`--scripts`).
+
+Run:  PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/enumerate.py [--unpinned|--all|--scripts|--summary]
+Baseline: 92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692, machine: owner macOS (arm64).
+"""
+import os
+for _v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
+           "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS", "VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS"):
+    os.environ.setdefault(_v, "1")
+import sys
+from collections import Counter
+sys.path.insert(0, "tests")
+import mutation_table as mt  # noqa: E402
+
+CELLS = ["coordinator", "optimizer", "thermal_model", "sysid", "defrost",
+         "flow_lift", "process_worker", "batchmath", "price_model", "tariff",
+         "grid_fee", "dhw_planner"]
+FILES = [mt.PRODUCTION / f"{c}.py" for c in CELLS]
+RELS = {mt.PKG + c + ".py" for c in CELLS}
+
+
+def sites():
+    budgets = mt.load_budgets()
+    inv = mt.inventory(sorted(FILES))
+    loose = {id(s) for s in mt.unpinned_sites(budgets, inv)}
+    disp = mt.dispositions(budgets)
+    out = []
+    for s in inv:
+        if id(s) in loose:
+            d = "unpinned"
+        else:
+            e = disp.get(s["anchor"], {})
+            if "killed_by" in e:
+                d = "killed_by:" + str(e.get("killed_by"))
+            else:
+                d = "triage:" + str(e.get("verdict"))
+        out.append((s, d))
+    return out
+
+
+def main():
+    mode = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "--unpinned"
+    if mode == "--scripts":
+        clos = mt.load_closures()
+        for s, files in sorted(clos.items()):
+            hit = sorted(f.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] for f in files if f in RELS)
+            if hit:
+                print(f"{s}\t{','.join(hit)}")
+        return
+    rows = sites()
+    if mode == "--summary":
+        c = Counter((s["file"].rsplit("/", 1)[-1], d.split(":")[0])
+                    for s, d in rows)
+        for k in sorted(c):
+            print(k[0], k[1], c[k])
+        print("RESULT sites_total=%d" % len(rows))
+        print("RESULT sites_unpinned=%d"
+              % sum(1 for _, d in rows if d.startswith("unpinned")))
+        return
+    for s, d in rows:
+        if mode == "--unpinned" and not d.startswith("unpinned"):
+            continue
+        print(f"{s['file']}:{s['line']}\t{s['kind']}\t{s['anchor']}\t{d}")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/finalize.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/finalize.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..949dde0fc5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/finalize.py
@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""D3-s1: run build_report.py, then write REPORT.md and carry its text in REPORT.json's report_md
+(run 1's subagent environment refused a .md write). Reads REPORT.json and state/ only."""
+import json, subprocess, sys
+from pathlib import Path
+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+
+
+def repo_root(start):
+    """The directory holding custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/manifest.json."""
+    from pathlib import Path
+    here = Path(start).resolve()
+    if here.is_file():
+        here = here.parent
+    marker = Path("custom_components") / "heatpump_optimizer" / "manifest.json"
+    for cand in (here, *here.parents):
+        if (cand / marker).is_file():
+            return cand
+    raise RuntimeError(f"no repository root above {start}")
+
+
+ROOT = repo_root(__file__)
+subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HERE / "build_report.py")], cwd=ROOT, check=True)
+r = json.loads((HERE / "REPORT.json").read_text())
+tab = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(HERE / "tabulate.py")], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
+m4 = json.loads((HERE / "m4_answers.json").read_text())
+L = ["# D3-s1 round 11 report (baseline 92d38ecb)", "",
+     "Seat D3-s1, two runs. Run 1: box B1, local run on the orchestrator machine (macOS arm64), resumed after a reboot at "
+     "about 17:40Z; contention load1 30-300 with other seats. Run 2: box D3R (Linux x86_64, nproc 4, Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz, "
+     "alone, load1 0.2-4.2), run inline in the box session: evidence restored (sha256 e2264708...), every driver's traced "
+     "baseline re-taken, null and positive controls re-run, C3C6 M22 re-driven, U1 started; halted by orchestrator STOP "
+     "(inbox command 1) after 4 U1 mutants.", "",
+     "Verdicts and counts are contention-immune; every wall/CPU number is provisional.", "",
+     "## Method", "",
+     "Universe: tests/mutation_table.py unpinned inventory sites in the 12 cell files (enumerate.py --unpinned). "
+     "Pre-screen (prescreen.py): each mutant driven over the fast scripts of its measured closure (recorded < 120 s) plus "
+     "tests/env_drift.py --all against HEAD^1 (production byte-identical to the baseline); reach-skip by traced baselines. "
+     "Survivors then go to a full-net complete (every closure script, no early stop). Null control LIVES; positive control 2/2 killed.", "",
+     "## Coverage", ""]
+for c in r["coverage"]:
+    L.append(f"- {c['step']}: universe {c['universe']}, examined {c['examined']}, not reached {len(c['not_reached'])} item line(s). Enumerator: `{c['enumerator']}`")
+L += ["", "## Findings", ""]
+for f in r["findings"]:
+    L.append(f"- {f['id']} ({f['step']}, {f['severity']}): {f['title']}")
+L += ["", "## Pre-screen tables (tabulate.py)", "", "```", tab.strip(), "```", "",
+      "## M4: the verifier's question per survivor", ""]
+for k, v in m4.items():
+    L.append(f"- `{k}`: {v}")
+L += ["", "## Non-findings", ""]
+for n in r["non_findings"]:
+    L.append(f"- {n['claim']}: {n['value']} (`{n['command']}`)")
+L += ["", "## Unfinished", ""]
+for u in r["unfinished"]:
+    L.append(f"- {u['step']}: {u['what']}")
+L += ["", "## Redispatched (C1-C9)", ""]
+for c in r["coverage"]:
+    L.append(f"- {c['step']}: " + ", ".join(f"{x['item']} {x['state']}" for x in c["redispatched"]))
+r["report_md"] = "\n".join(L) + "\n"
+(HERE / "REPORT.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1) + "\n")
+(HERE / "REPORT.md").write_text(r["report_md"])
+print("RESULT report_md_lines=%d findings=%d" % (len(L), len(r["findings"])))
diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/findings-local.json b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/findings-local.json
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..c9066bf45b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/findings-local.json
@@ -0,0 +1,48 @@
+[
+ {
+  "id": "D3-s1-01",
+  "scope": "D3-s1",
+  "step": "D3.M5",
+  "title": "Mutation lane drives env_drift --all on every cell mutant, though its capture never executes 681 of the 1260 unpinned sites",
+  "severity": "medium",
+  "claim": "Of the 1260 unpinned inventory sites in the D3-s1 cell files, 681 lie on executable lines that env_drift.py's only production-executing step (the `--capture <tree> <out> --all` child) never executes, yet tests/mutation_table.py's reach rule can skip env_drift for none of them (gate_skippable=0), so every such mutant pays a full `env_drift.py --all` golden capture that cannot change.",
+  "mechanism": "env_drift.py starts its capture child with `env[\"PYTHONPATH\"] = <tree>/tests/hastub` (tests/env_drift.py, the capture loop in main), which drops the reach hook's directory, so the child leaves no reach record (processes started 3, recorded 1); the parent also starts git/file/uname. mutation_table.reach_problems refuses any run that starts a non-Python process or loses a record, so env_drift's reach row is never usable and reach_skip never skips it.",
+  "evidence": {
+   "command": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_envdrift_reach.py",
+   "harness_path": "dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_envdrift_reach.py",
+   "value": 681,
+   "unit": "unpinned cell sites whose line the env_drift --capture --all child never executes, all still driven (gate_skippable=0)",
+   "baseline_sha": "92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692",
+   "machine": "owner macOS arm64 (Darwin), venv-ci CPython 3.14",
+   "cpu_or_wall": "count",
+   "contention_note": "Counts are contention-immune. The traced baselines were taken while another D3 seat (D3-s3), verifier seats and the orchestrator's beat jobs ran on this machine (load1 30-300); the env_drift wall quoted (602.8 s for one --all run) is provisional.",
+   "tolerance": "exact",
+   "load1": 43.2,
+   "thread_factor": 1.0
+  },
+  "instrumented_symbol": "tests/mutation_table.py:reach_skip (and reach_problems) on tests/env_drift.py's traced baseline; tests/env_drift.py:capture_tree traced in its --capture child",
+  "perturbation": {

+{
+ "id": "D3-s1-52",
+ "scope": "D3-s1",
+ "step": "D3.M5",
+ "title": "card_drift.mjs inherits plan_view.py closure, yet compares two cards over one payload: no cell edit can move it",
+ "severity": "low",
+ "claim": "tests/closure.py's _widen unions tests/plan_view.py's closure into tests/card_drift.mjs's, so 11 of the 12 D3-s1 cell files schedule card_drift on every one-file diff (closure.select), yet card_drift renders the working tree's card and the ref's card against ONE shared plan payload, so a production edit that changes that payload (sha256 differs) leaves 0 of its 45 states moved, while a one-token card edit moves 44.",
+ "mechanism": "PRODUCERS = {'tests/card.mjs': [plan_view], 'tests/card_drift.mjs': [plan_view]} is used twice: as a selection-ordering edge (a selected card script needs its producer first: sound) and, in _widen, as a closure union ('anything that can change the payload can change what they test'). The union is sound for card.mjs, whose checks are absolute assertions over the payload, and unsound for card_drift.mjs, whose verdict is byte-equality of two card renders that both read the same payload in one process (tests/card_drift.mjs header, renderAll over makeSide(treeSrc) and makeSide(baseSrc)). A cell-file diff changes only the payload, which both sides share, and touches neither the card source nor a solver fixture (claimsAreThisBranchs), so the comparison is an identity.",
+ "evidence": {
+  "command": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py",
+  "harness_path": "dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py",
+  "value": 0,
+  "unit": "card_drift.mjs states moved (of 45) under each of two payload-changing production edits (prod_small x1.0001, prod_large x1.5 on thermal_model.py's room-temperature step; payload_changed=1 for both); cell_diffs_selecting_card_drift=11, card_drift_cell_closure_edges=11",
+  "baseline_sha": "92d38ecb640bd462f2e19c0814d0f0b7df1ee692",
+  "machine": "box D3-m5: Linux 6.18 x86_64, nproc 4, Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz, venv-ci CPython 3.14.7 (numpy 2.5.4, scipy 1.18.1), node v22.23.5, alone on the box",
+  "cpu_or_wall": "count",
+  "contention_note": "Counts are contention-immune. Measured alone on box D3-m5 (load1 0.7-1.1). The cost figure quoted (card_drift.mjs 4.0 s wall / 5.1 s CPU per gate run, from m5_gate_table.py, GATE_JOBS=1 shape) is provisional.",
+  "tolerance": "exact",
+  "load1": 1.07,
+  "thread_factor": 1.0
+ },
+ "instrumented_symbol": "tests/card_drift.mjs verdict (DRIFT/CLAIMED/identical lines) over tests/plan_view.py's payload, driven with production custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/thermal_model.py edited in a private worktree; tests/closure.py:select and tests/closure.py:_widen (PRODUCERS union) for the scheduling edges",
+ "perturbation": {
+  "change": "the harness's `card` arm: one CSS token of custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/www/heatpump-optimizer-card.js (`ha-card { padding: 12px ...}` -> `13px`) in the same worktree, payload unchanged",
+  "expected_direction": "up",
+  "observed_value": "moved 0 -> 44 of 45 (card_drift rc 0 -> 1); the two production arms stay at 0 with payload_changed=1"
+ },
+ "metric_definition": "States tests/card_drift.mjs HEAD^1 reports moved (DRIFT or CLAIMED lines, stdout to a file) on a payload plan_view.py writes from a worktree with one edit applied.",
+ "phenomenon_property": "A differential gate driver that renders both of its sides from one shared producer output inherits that producer's closure, so every diff that can only change the shared input schedules it, and it can never move.",
+ "seam_rule": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py --select-only",
+ "null_control": {
+  "command": "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py",
+  "value": "base arm moved=0 identical=45; card arm moved=44 (the gate moves when the thing it compares moves); card.mjs, the non-differential consumer of the same payload, keeps its producer edge (it reads payload values absolutely)",
+  "note": "The two production arms change the payload (sha256 f769f5bd... -> 8cee8f3f... and df892bf5...), so the zero is not an unchanged input. Kill matrix corroboration (m5_matrix.py table, every closure script on 38 cell mutants, no early stop): card_drift.mjs ran on the 10 whose line plan_view executes (28 reach-skipped) and killed 0; card.mjs likewise 0 of 10; plan_view.py 0 of 10."
+ },
+ "reproduction_steps": [
+  "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py",
+  "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_card_drift_payload.py --select-only",
+  "PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D3/s1/m5_matrix.py table -v | grep card_drift"
+ ],
+ "proposed_fix_scope": "tests/closure.py: keep card_drift.mjs's PRODUCERS entry for selection ORDER (a card diff still runs plan_view first) but stop _widen from unioning the producer's closure into card_drift.mjs's; re-derive its closures.json entry (its raw trace was 6 files, #527). Verify with this harness's --select-only (11 -> 0) and the card arm (still 44).",
+ "files": [
+  "tests/closure.py",
+  "tests/closures.json"
+ ],
+ "stop_rule_class": "hygiene",
+ "class_guess": "new"

index 0000000000..1bee104d68

@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+{
+ "0318c921405fefbe": "dhw_planner.py:473 DhwPlanner._dhw_planning_prices, `if space_demand is not None:` off: the co-optimisation replan no longer subtracts the space profile from the PV surplus, so DHW is priced against surplus the space heating already took. Should fail: a features.py DHW-PV check with a known space_demand that consumes part of the surplus (DHW blended price must rise vs the no-space arm).",
+ "050fdc4a20eba212": "thermal_model.py:169 _holiday_dhw_windows, `if not spec:` off: an unset holiday window spec reaches parse_windows; if that returns [] for an empty spec the holiday day gets NO DHW windows instead of falling back. Should fail: a from_config check with holiday DHW windows unset and a holiday date in the horizon (windows on that day equal the default).",
+ "0c3e91a6a349409a": "flow_lift.py:47 FLOW_BIAS_ALPHA 0.1 -> 0.2: the seeded EWMA weights each new residual twice as hard. Should fail: a FlowCurveBias.observe check past FLOW_BIAS_MIN_SAMPLES that pins bias_k after one more residual to (1-alpha)*b + alpha*r.",
+ "121362d48b408236": "grid_fee.py:173 _parse_rule, `if not sep:` off: a rule line with no '= rate' no longer raises GridFeeError; rate_token is the whole line and float() raises ValueError -> 'Bad rate' instead. Error class unchanged, message changes; near-equivalent. Should fail: a config-flow validation check asserting the 'has no = rate part' message for 'Mon 06-22'.",
+ "3885e472b8297a90": "flow_lift.py:183 FlowCurveBias.observe, non-finite guard off: a NaN/inf supply reading is folded; np.clip(NaN) is NaN, so bias_k becomes NaN. Should fail: a check feeding observe(nan, 35.0) and asserting bias_k unchanged and finite (finite_boundary.py drives persisted leaves, not live observations).",
+ "460217277822d5bd": "sysid.py:610 slab_mode_tau_fast, unset-constant guard off: with c_r/c_s/k_s zero the expression divides by zero (ZeroDivisionError or inf) instead of returning 0.0. Should fail: slab_mode_tau_fast(0,0,0) == 0.0 and the #991 gate refusing an unconfigured slab plant with its own reason.",
+ "4b3795aece73ba73": "price_model.py:201 PriceShapeModel.observe_day, non-finite day guard off: a day with a NaN/inf hour is folded and the shape goes non-finite. Should fail: observe_day(day, [..nan..]) returns False and leaves shapes/days unchanged.",
+ "4e2df5f23e4eff29": "coordinator.py:422 _plain_types dict branch off. Full net: KILLED by tests/features.py ('numpy scalars and arrays are flattened to plain Python, recursively'). No gap; the fast closure scripts do not pin it.",
+ "61f74c4474262dad": "coordinator.py:687 fenced-step logging, first-occurrence test off: every failure logs at DEBUG, never the first WARNING. Should fail: a check that a fenced step's first exception logs one WARNING and a repeat logs DEBUG.",
+ "639d439d71b731ce": "dhw_planner.py:75 _dhw_windows_at, holiday flag lookup off: holiday is always False, so holiday DHW windows never apply in the planner. Should fail: a planner run with holiday_flags True on a step and holiday windows differing from the default (features.py tests windows_for_day directly, not this lookup).",
+ "65f121eb047174ad": "optimizer.py:773 _holiday_flags_for, empty-set early return off: returns an all-False array instead of None. Downstream an all-False flag array selects the same windows as None: equivalent in the plan, differs only in object identity. Equivalent.",
+ "73bc722df73caecb": "price_model.py:198 observe_day, 24-hour length guard off: a 23- or 25-hour (DST) day is folded; values.reshape/shape update then misaligns or raises. Should fail: observe_day on a 23-value list returns False (the docstring's partial-day rule).",
+ "a0605da712a6a070": "defrost.py:419 DefrostDerate.observe_duty range guard off. Full net: KILLED by tests/features.py ('a duty outside [0, 1] is refused, not folded into the bucket'). No gap; only features.py pins it.",
+ "a35e03bd09f563c7": "sysid.py:677 slab_mode_one_state_identifiability, unset-constant guard off: an unconfigured slab plant is evaluated (division by zero or a wrong verdict) instead of refused with 'slab constants not configured'. Should fail: the identifiability check on c_r=c_s=k_s=0 returns (False, that reason).",
+ "bdcf7589b0a0a6df": "coordinator.py:539 _parse_ecl110_state, nested command.displace fallback off: an ECL110 payload carrying displace only under 'command' parses to None. Should fail: a parse check on {'command': {'displace': 3}} returning displace 3.0.",
+ "fb16c7b0cbbfc63d": "tariff.py:64 _window_slot, fold transfer off for sub-hour/hourly windows: both passes of the autumn DST repeated hour get the same window key, one accumulator swallows two metered hours and the peak is diluted (the comment's own failure). Ledger: the CMP_BOUND sibling on this line is killed_by tests/features.py (dst_checks.py runs under it); this GUARD_OFF is unpinned. Should fail: a features/dst_checks check that the two passes of 02:00-03:00 on the autumn change get distinct keys at window 60.",
+ "0e172028a23d9372": "sysid.py:2246 (R10 M27) `and` -> `or`: the drift refusal fires whenever ua_ss > 0, so every completed step test is refused as 'sensor drift collapsed into heat-loss'. Should fail: a sysid step-test check whose steady-state UA agrees within 10 % completes.",
+ "2719aef4cbb8b464": "price_model.py:337 (R10 M25) `level <= 0.0` -> `< 0.0`: at level exactly 0 the gate returns 0 x min-shape instead of None. Should fail: expected-minimum check at level 0.0 returning None.",
+ "66f8a4fb50e0b1f3": "defrost.py:783 (R10 M32) `and not` -> `or not`: a defrost flag seen while already defrosting counts a new event each observation. Ledger pins this site killed_by tests/features.py; fast net cannot see it.",
+ "8e82d7a0b3617003": "sysid.py:1549 (R10 M26) `hour >= start` -> `hour > start`: the first hour of a midnight-wrapping night window is excluded. Should fail: a gate check at now.hour == cfg.start_hour for a wrapping window returning in_window True.",
+ "aae7c9c380c3c5cf": "sysid.py:1593 (R10 M28) `and` -> `or`: a step size passes if either the peak or the final excursion fits. Ledger pins this BOOLOP killed_by tests/features.py.",
+ "ad5900dadd86e9f9": "tariff.py:64 (R10 M29) `window <= 60` -> `< 60`: hourly windows (the common DSO case) lose the DST fold transfer. Ledger pins this CMP_BOUND killed_by tests/features.py.",
+ "d931ab195b940b0c": "tariff.py:744 (R10 M31) `k <= 0` -> `k < 0`: k == 0 proceeds to max(1, ...) and returns the top-1 sum instead of 0.0. Should fail: top_k_sum(values, 0) == 0.0.",
+ "fc395b83eeb1ddbf": "price_model.py:532 (R10 M33) min -> max over known_count/len: indexes past step_start_times when known_count exceeds it (IndexError) or reads unknown steps. Should fail: a shape-mean check with known_count > len(step_start_times).",
+ "0911281eca895664": "dhw_planner.py:1559 (R10 M19) max -> min in the shortfall price: shortfall slack priced 1000 x (min|price| + 1) instead of max. Equivalent while 1000 x (min + 1) still exceeds every real price/COP; differs only when the cheapest step is near zero and a step price exceeds 1000. Should fail: an LP check with a price spread above 1000x the minimum where the shortfall must stay last resort.",
+ "22b5ec8775d5bd50": "thermal_model.py:2593 (R10 M07) max(dt, 1e-6) -> min(dt, 1e-6): buffer availability divided by 1e-6 h, so the draw is never scaled down. Should fail: a buffer-draw check where drawn exceeds available heat and the floor/radiator draws must be scaled.",
+ "5cc84148fa68bda1": "grid_fee.py:383 (R10 M21) `rate < lowest` -> `<=`: on a tie the source label flips 'fixed' -> 'rules' with the same value. Should fail: a lowest-fee check on a schedule whose rule rate equals the fixed fee asserting source 'fixed'.",
+ "5e8d48eff7e4fa8d": "coordinator.py:8806 (R10 M04) `tariff.enabled and factor > 0` -> `or`: a disabled tariff with factor > 0 adds a peak-threshold candidate to the guard. Should fail: a power-guard check with the tariff disabled asserting only the fuse candidate applies.",
+ "a4b00ac3ca662eec": "thermal_model.py:835 (R10 M03) `swing <= 0` -> `< 0`: at swing 0 the cosine term is multiplied by 0, so the result is identical. Equivalent.",
+ "c38d53ab787ddbfa": "price_model.py:252 (R10 M34) mean <= 1e-6 -> < 1e-6: only a day whose mean is exactly 1e-6 is now folded (dividing hour means by ~1e-6). Near-equivalent boundary. Should fail: observe_quarter_day on a 96-value day with mean exactly 1e-6 returns False.",
+ "a0b3b28854fa500c": "flow_lift.py:188 (R10 M35) samples < MIN -> <= MIN: the sample at index FLOW_BIAS_MIN_SAMPLES still uses the running mean instead of the EWMA, so the switch to EWMA is one sample late. Should fail: a FlowCurveBias.observe check that pins bias_k after exactly MIN+1 samples to the EWMA update.",
+ "95779f9d6d71c50d": "grid_fee.py:355 (R10 M36) abs(rate) > worst -> >=: on a tie between a rule rate and the fixed fee, source flips 'fixed' -> 'rules' with the same value (sibling of M21 at L383). Should fail: a worst-fee check on a schedule whose rule rate equals the fixed fee asserting source 'fixed'."
+}
\ No newline at end of file

+ "acc8fa3942789f45": "thermal_model.py:270 ThermalParameters.clamp, the non-finite/below-floor thermal-mass guard off (`if False:`): a NaN, inf or sub-floor house/lower-floor thermal mass is kept instead of clamped to THERMAL_MASS_FLOOR. Should fail: a clamp check that sets thermal_mass to NaN and to 0 and asserts both come back as THERMAL_MASS_FLOOR (finite_boundary.py or a thermal_model unit check). Survived 15 fast drivers incl. finite_boundary.py and env_drift.py --all on this box.",
+ "23621370731667b7": "defrost.py:559 DefrostDerate.from_dict, the `elif any(k in data for k in (\"duty\", \"duty_counts\"))` corrupt-v2 branch off: a v2 store whose measured half is unreadable is read as a v1 store, so `reset` stays 0 and `migrated` follows the factors list -- the corrupt store is reported as an upgrade and its reset count is lost. Should fail: a from_dict check feeding a v2 payload with an unreadable duty table and asserting reset == n_t*n_h and migrated is False. env_drift.py was relaxed-skipped (its capture never executes the line); the deferred slow drivers (harness_headers, boost_drift_replay, entities, features) are owed to the full net.",
+ "6e6026d857732e96": "tariff.py:595 mask_active (R10 C3/C6 M22), `or` -> `and`: a tariff with only a month mask (months set, no peak_hours/weekdays_only offpeak mask) reads as mask-inactive, so the #13 month mask stops changing what a window counts at.
