+"""Null-control fixture: one background solve, behind an in-flight guard."""
+
+
+async def _await_optimize(hass, opt, inputs):  # infrastructure: excluded
+    return await hass.async_add_executor_job(opt.solve, inputs)
+
+
+class Coord:
+    def __init__(self):
+        self._whatif_task = None
+
+    async def async_whatif(self, overrides):
+        if self._whatif_task is not None and not self._whatif_task.done():
+            return None
+        return await _await_optimize(self.hass, self.opt, overrides)
diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/D14/background/enumerate.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/D14/background/enumerate.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..ff89e5e087
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/D14/background/enumerate.py
@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+"""D14 sweep, class N-unbudgeted-background: list every background-work submit seam.
+
+A seam is a call site in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/**/*.py, inside a
+function, of a primitive that runs work off the event loop or starts a solve:
+    _await_optimize, _await_process, _await_off_loop      (the solve worker / executor)
+    async_simulate                                        (a full what-if solve, 1-3 jobs)
+    async_add_executor_job, run_in_executor               (HA / asyncio executor)
+The infrastructure that implements those primitives (their own bodies) is
+excluded.  For each seam it reports:
+  enclosing   the function the call sits in
+  roots       the package functions that (transitively, by name) reach it, cut
+              at known trigger roots: the cycle (_async_update_data /
+              async_run_optimization), services, setup, the debugger
+  guard       tokens in the enclosing function or any caller on the path that
+              bound in-flight work or a budget: `_running`, `.done()`, `Lock`,
+              `in_flight`/`inflight`, `budget`, `limited_answer`, `last_at`,
+              `semaphore`, a `return` under an `if` reading one of them
+              (a heuristic, printed for the disposition, not a verdict)
+Run:  python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/background/enumerate.py [--root DIR] [--json]
+"""
+import ast
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+
+args = sys.argv[1:]
+ROOT = args[args.index("--root") + 1] if "--root" in args else "custom_components/heatpump_optimizer"
+PRIMS = {"_await_optimize", "_await_process", "_await_off_loop", "async_simulate",
+         "async_add_executor_job", "run_in_executor"}
+INFRA = {"_await_optimize", "_await_process", "_await_off_loop", "_run_in_process"}
+GUARD = re.compile(r"_running\b|\.done\(\)|Lock\(|_lock\b|in_?flight|budget|limited_answer|last_at|[Ss]emaphore|_pending_task|_task is not None")
+ROOTS = re.compile(r"^(_async_update_data|async_run_optimization|async_setup.*|_async_setup.*|handle_.*|_handle_.*|async_handle.*|.*_service.*)$")
+
+
+def callee(n):
+    f = n.func
+    return f.attr if isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) else f.id if isinstance(f, ast.Name) else None
+
+
+def code_only(n):
+    """The function's code with comments and docstrings dropped, so a guard
+    token must be code (a comment saying 'budget' is not a budget)."""
+    import copy
+    m = copy.deepcopy(n)
+    for x in ast.walk(m):
+        b = getattr(x, "body", None)
+        if isinstance(b, list) and b and isinstance(b[0], ast.Expr) and isinstance(getattr(b[0], "value", None), ast.Constant) \
+                and isinstance(b[0].value.value, str):
+            x.body = b[1:] or [ast.Pass()]
+    return ast.unparse(m)
+
+
+def collect():
+    funcs = {}  # (file, name) -> (node, src)
+    for dp, dn, fn in os.walk(ROOT):
+        dn[:] = sorted(d for d in dn if d not in ("www", "translations", "__pycache__"))
+        for f in sorted(fn):
+            if not f.endswith(".py"):
+                continue
+            p = os.path.join(dp, f)
+            text = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
+            for n in ast.walk(ast.parse(text)):
+                if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
+                    funcs.setdefault((p, n.name), (n, code_only(n)))
+    return funcs
+
+
+def direct_calls(node):
+    """Calls in this function body, not inside nested defs (those are their own functions)."""
+    out = []
+    stack = list(ast.iter_child_nodes(node))
+    while stack:
+        x = stack.pop()
+        if isinstance(x, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda)) and x is not node:
+            if isinstance(x, ast.Lambda):
+                stack.extend(ast.iter_child_nodes(x))
+            continue
+        if isinstance(x, ast.Call):
+            out.append(x)
+        stack.extend(ast.iter_child_nodes(x))
+    return out
+
+
+def seams():
+    funcs = collect()
+    callers = {}
+    for (p, name), (node, _) in funcs.items():
+        for c in direct_calls(node):
+            nm = callee(c)
+            if nm:
+                callers.setdefault(nm, set()).add((p, name))
+        # functools.partial(self._x, ...) / references passed as values count as calls
+        for x in ast.walk(node):
+            if isinstance(x, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(x.ctx, ast.Load) and x.attr.startswith(("_maybe", "_async", "async_")):
+                callers.setdefault(x.attr, set()).add((p, name))
+
+    def path_up(name, seen=None, depth=0):
+        seen = seen if seen is not None else set()
+        if depth > 8 or name in seen:
+            return set(), set()
+        seen.add(name)
+        if ROOTS.match(name):
+            return {name}, set()
+        roots, guards = set(), set()
+        for (p, caller) in callers.get(name, ()):
+            src = funcs[(p, caller)][1]
+            g = set(GUARD.findall(src))
+            r, gg = path_up(caller, seen, depth + 1)
+            roots |= r or {caller + "(no root)"}
+            guards |= {f"{caller}:{t}" for t in g} | gg
+        return roots, guards
+
+    out = []
+    for (p, name), (node, src) in sorted(funcs.items()):
+        if name in INFRA:
+            continue
+        for c in direct_calls(node):
+            nm = callee(c)
+            if nm in PRIMS:
+                arg0 = ""
+                if c.args:
+                    a = c.args[-1] if nm in ("_await_process", "_await_off_loop", "async_add_executor_job") and len(c.args) >= 2 else c.args[0]
+                    a = c.args[1] if nm in ("_await_process", "_await_off_loop", "async_add_executor_job", "run_in_executor") and len(c.args) >= 2 else a
+                    arg0 = ast.unparse(a)[:60]
+                own = sorted(set(GUARD.findall(src)))
+                roots, guards = path_up(name)
+                out.append({"file": p, "line": c.lineno, "enclosing": name, "primitive": nm, "job": arg0,
+                            "own_guard": own, "path_guards": sorted(guards)[:6], "roots": sorted(roots)[:6]})
+    return out
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    s = seams()
+    if "--json" in args:
+        print(json.dumps(s, indent=1))
+    else:
+        for x in s:
+            print(f"{x['file']}:{x['line']}  {x['enclosing']} -> {x['primitive']}({x['job']})  own_guard={x['own_guard']}  roots={x['roots']}  path_guards={x['path_guards']}")
+        print(f"RESULT seams={len(s)} count")
+        print(f"RESULT unguarded={sum(not x['own_guard'] for x in s)} count")
diff --git a/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/D14/background/probe_burst.py b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/D14/background/probe_burst.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..53c9d2c046
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/D14/background/probe_burst.py
@@ -0,0 +1,117 @@
+"""D14 sweep N-unbudgeted-background: a burst of K user-triggered background
+jobs through one seam, counted at the production worker submit.
+
+Metric: entries into coordinator._run_in_process (each holds _PROCESS_LOCK for
+one job) started by K concurrent calls of a seam, split by job callable
+(__qualname__), plus multi-start solver entries (optimizer._multi_start_minimize)
+the burst causes, and the latency of a scheduled solve submitted right behind
+the burst over its solo latency.  Seams:
+  diagnose   coordinator.async_diagnose_interval (diagnose_interval service / button)
+  whatif     coordinator.async_simulate(steady=True)  (positive control: D9-s1-03)
+Arms: --seam S --k K ; --guard adds an in-memory in-flight guard on the seam
+(one-line: a second concurrent call returns at once) -> jobs must fall to the
+K=1 level.  Null control: K=1.
+Run:  PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/background/probe_burst.py --seam diagnose --k 4
+Route and fixture: dev/audit/rounds/round11/D9/s1/d9s1lib.py (the D9-s1 harness library), the shipped worker.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+for _v in ("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS", "MKL_NUM_THREADS",
+           "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS", "VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS"):
+    os.environ.setdefault(_v, "1")
+
+import argparse  # noqa: E402
+import asyncio  # noqa: E402
+import collections  # noqa: E402
+import sys  # noqa: E402
+import time  # noqa: E402
+from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor  # noqa: E402
+from datetime import timedelta  # noqa: E402
+
+sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "D9", "s1"))
+import d9s1lib as L  # noqa: E402
+
+
+async def burst(seam: str, k: int, guard: bool):
+    from heatpump_optimizer import coordinator as cm
+    from heatpump_optimizer import optimizer as om
+    from heatpump_optimizer.const import SIMULATE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS
+    from homeassistant.util import dt as dtu
+    from profiles import house
+
+    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+    pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=8)
+    hass = L.make_loop_hass(loop, pool)
+    dtu.freeze(L.CYCLE_NOW)
+    coord = L.make_coordinator(hass, dict(house(two_zone=True, dhw=True)), entry_id=f"bb_{seam}_{k}_{int(guard)}")
+    for i in range(2):
+        now = L.CYCLE_NOW + timedelta(minutes=30 * i)
+        dtu.freeze(now)
+        L.feed(coord, now)
+        coord.data = await coord._async_update_data()
+
+    jobs = collections.Counter()
+    real_run = cm._run_in_process
+
+    def counting_run(fn, args):
+        jobs[getattr(fn, "__qualname__", "?")] += 1
+        return real_run(fn, args)
+
+    cm._run_in_process = counting_run
+    inflight = {"n": 0}
+
+    async def one(i):
+        if guard and inflight["n"] > 0:
+            return {"rate_limited": True}
+        inflight["n"] += 1
+        try:
+            if seam == "diagnose":
+                return await coord.async_diagnose_interval()
+            return await coord.async_simulate({"target_temp": 20.0 + 0.1 * i}, steady=True)
+        finally:
+            inflight["n"] -= 1
+
+    base = L.CYCLE_NOW + timedelta(minutes=30, seconds=60)
+    try:
+        tasks = []
+        for i in range(k):
+            dtu.freeze(base + timedelta(seconds=(SIMULATE_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS + 0.05) * i))
+            tasks.append(asyncio.create_task(one(i)))
+            await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
+        opt, inp, _ = L.make_solve("two_zone_dhw")
+        t = time.perf_counter()
+        sched = asyncio.create_task(cm._await_optimize(hass, opt, inp))
+        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
+        await sched
+        sched_s = time.perf_counter() - t
+        # let any refresh the seam requested run out
+        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
+    finally:
+        cm._run_in_process = real_run
+        cm._shutdown_process_pool()
+        pool.shutdown()
+    jobs["optimize_in_process"] -= 1 if k >= 0 else 0  # the scheduled solve's own
+    return jobs, sched_s
+
+
+def main():
+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    ap.add_argument("--seam", default="diagnose", choices=("diagnose", "whatif"))
+    ap.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=4)
+    ap.add_argument("--guard", action="store_true")
+    a = ap.parse_args()
+    _, solo = asyncio.run(burst(a.seam, 0, False))
+    print(f"RESULT k0.scheduled_solve_s={solo:.3f} s")
+    for k in ((1, a.k) if not a.guard else (a.k,)):
+        jobs, s = asyncio.run(burst(a.seam, k, a.guard))
+        tag = f"{a.seam}.k{k}" + (".guard" if a.guard else "")
+        total = sum(v for v in jobs.values() if v > 0)
+        print(f"RESULT {tag}.worker_jobs={total} count  by_job={dict((n, v) for n, v in jobs.items() if v)}")
+        print(f"RESULT {tag}.solve_jobs={max(0, jobs['optimize_in_process'])} count")
+        print(f"RESULT {tag}.scheduled_latency_over_solo={s / solo:.2f} ratio")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

index 0000000000..ce04dcf10d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/dev/audit/rounds/round11/sweep/N-unbudgeted-background/sweep-N-unbudgeted-background.md
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# Round 11 class sweep: N-unbudgeted-background (box SW4)
+
+**Class mechanism (judge):** background solves (what-ifs, advisors) stack onto
+the main solve with no per-cycle budget or in-flight guard, so a burst
+multiplies worker jobs and delays the scheduled solve. `N-unbudgeted-background`
+has no entry in `dev/audit/config/bugclasses.json` at the register tip: it is a
+new class this round (nearest P10), effectively `open`.
+
+**Findings in the class:**
+
+- **D9-s1-02** (weakened, low): the fuse advisor plus its steady pair plus the
+  price tile stack after the main solve in one cycle.
+- **D9-s1-03** (verified, medium): user what-ifs queue 3 solves each; the 3 s
+  limiter has no in-flight guard.
+
+**Result:** 17 seams; **0 instances beyond the findings**, 5 judged sites,
+4 guarded, 8 not applicable. `instances` = 0.
+
+## Detector (D14 step 3)
+
+### Static enumerator
+
+`dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/background/enumerate.py` lists every call, inside
+a package function, of a primitive that runs work off the event loop or starts
+a solve:
+
+- `_await_optimize`, `_await_process` and `_await_off_loop`. All three reach
+  the one persistent worker under `_PROCESS_LOCK` (`coordinator.py:2072`);
+  `_await_off_loop` falls back to the executor only on
+  `ProcessWorkerUnavailable`.
+- `async_simulate`, which is 1 to 3 full solves.
+- `async_add_executor_job` and `run_in_executor`.
+
+The bodies of the primitives themselves are excluded. Each seam carries:
+
+- its enclosing function;
+- name-based trigger roots, which are approximate;
+- guard tokens in code only, with comments and docstrings stripped. A comment
+  saying "never on its budget" at `coordinator.py:9001` and `:10695` matched
+  before the strip and is not a guard.
+
+The output is in `D14/background/seams.txt`.
+
+### Runtime probe
+
+`probe_burst.py --seam S --k K [--guard]` drives K concurrent calls of a seam on
+the shipped worker, using the D9-s1 library `d9s1lib`. It counts
+`_run_in_process` entries by job and reports the latency of a scheduled solve
+submitted behind the burst, over its solo latency. The finding's own
+`h_solves_per_cycle.py` (output in `D14/background/spc_out.txt`) supplies the
+per-path cycle counts.
+
+### Controls and perturbation
+
+- **Positive control:**
+  - The enumerator lists every judged site: `_maybe_run_fuse_advisor`
+    (`coordinator.py:9004`), `_maybe_refresh_price_tile` (`:10709`),
+    `async_simulate` (`:11239`), `_held_solve` (`:11245`) and
+    `handle_simulate_plan` (`services.py:775`).
+  - `probe_burst.py --seam whatif --k 4` re-finds D9-s1-03 on this tree:
+    **12 worker jobs, scheduled solve 11.10x solo**. At K=1 it gives 3 jobs
+    and 3.56x. The finding read 12.4x and the judge 12.04x.
+  - `h_solves_per_cycle.py --cycles 4 --arms default,tiles_fuse` shows the
+    D9-s1-02 stacking. In the default arm every cycle has 2 multi-start
+    entries and only main jobs. In tiles_fuse the worst cycle has 9 entries,
+    with fuse_advisor 1+2 jobs and price_tile 4 jobs (5.43 s CPU against the
+    main solve's 4.40 s).
+- **Null control:**
+  - The enumerator on `D14/background/clean_fixture` (one background solve
+    behind a `.done()` in-flight check) gives 1 seam, **0 unguarded**.
+  - The probe at K=1 gives 3 jobs per what-if.
+- **Perturbation:**
+  - Replacing the fixture's guard line with `if False:` gives 1 unguarded;
+    restoring it gives 0.
+  - `probe_burst.py --seam whatif --k 4 --guard` adds a one-line in-flight
+    guard in memory and drops the burst to **3 jobs, 3.80x**, the K=1 level.
+
+## Disposition (D14 step 4)
+
+### Judged sites (5, `beyond_finding: false`)
+
+| seam | finding |
+|---|---|
+| `coordinator.py:9004` `_maybe_run_fuse_advisor` | D9-s1-02 |
+| `coordinator.py:10709` `_maybe_refresh_price_tile` | D9-s1-02 |
+| `coordinator.py:11239` `async_simulate` | D9-s1-03 |
+| `coordinator.py:11245` `async_simulate._held_solve` (the steady pair) | D9-s1-03 |
+| `services.py:775` `handle_simulate_plan` (the service entry) | D9-s1-03 |
+
+### Guarded (4)
+
+| seam | guard |
+|---|---|
+| `coordinator.py:6430` `async_run_optimization`, the main solve | `if self._optimization_running:` records a re-run and returns (`coordinator.py:6359-6363`), so concurrent requests coalesce into one |
+| `coordinator.py:10675` `async_diagnose_interval` (diagnose_interval service and button, no in-flight flag) | Measured: `probe_burst.py --seam diagnose --k 4` gives 4 `diagnose_record` jobs, but still **1 solve job** with a scheduled-solve latency of **1.44x** (K=1: 1.56x). The refresh each call requests is coalesced by the coordinator's refresh and the running flag above. `diagnose_record` makes no optimizer call: it runs 1 + len(SWAPPABLE) single-step `simulate_step` calls (`diagnosis.py:75-156`), not a solve. A burst therefore does not stack solves. |
+| `debugger.py:325` `_solver_smoke` (`async_simulate({}, limited=False)`) | Runs once per debug-collection stop: `_async_finish` is spawned by `finalize`. A second stop raises `ServiceValidationError` (`debugger.py:717`), the button is available only while `not collector.final` (`button.py:235`), and self-tests are bounded by `SELF_TEST_BUDGET` (`debugger.py:76`). Measured at 1 worker job per trigger. |
+| `coordinator.py:2166` `_sysid_step_off_loop` | Once per cycle, inside `async_run_optimization` under the same running flag |
+
+### Not applicable (8)
+
+**Fixed per-cycle count, non-solve jobs (3):**
+
+- `coordinator.py:1080` `_replay_interval` (learner interval replays).
+- `coordinator.py:2206` `_with_sensor_advisor`, once per successful cycle at
+  `coordinator.py:6141`.
+- `coordinator.py:2184` `estimate`, the away-recovery estimate.
+
+A fixed set of learners or advisors runs once per cycle; no user action or
+burst multiplies them. Measured: all `_async_update_data`-path jobs together
+are 7 worker jobs and **0.0087 s CPU over 4 cycles** in both arms, which is
+negligible against the main solve's ~1.1 s per cycle.
+
+**One-shot (2):**
+
+- `coordinator.py:1959` `_stop` (worker shutdown).
+- `frontend.py:193` `async_register_frontend` (setup).
+
+**Not a solve and not the worker (3):**
+
+- `debugger.py:595` `_read` (store files).
+- `debugger.py:664` and `:672` `_async_replay`: one recorder query plus up to
+  4 replay-document builds on HA's executor (`fit_replay`,
+  `debugger.py:462-472`), triggered by a diagnostics download, with no
+  optimizer call.
+
+`_async_replay` has no in-flight guard either, but it neither holds
+`_PROCESS_LOCK` nor delays the scheduled solve. **It is noted for D9
+(executor load on repeated downloads), not counted in this class.**
+
+## Proposed barrier (D14 step 5)
+
+- **Runtime:** a `tests/` check built from `probe_burst.py`. For every seam the
+  enumerator returns whose trigger is a user action or a per-cycle advisor,
+  assert that a K=4 burst starts no more worker solve jobs than K=1 (an
+  in-flight guard). For the cycle tail, assert that background solve CPU per
+  cycle is at most a declared fraction of the main solve's.
+- **Static:** `enumerate.py` as a lint that refuses a new seam whose path
+  carries no guard token unless it is listed with its reason.
+- **Cost:** about 60 s for the whatif arm and about 10 s for diagnose. The
+  enumerator takes under 1 s.
+- **Count:** with 0 beyond-finding instances, the class is the two judged
+  findings, which share the cycle tail and `async_simulate`. The fix is one
+  in-flight guard on `async_simulate`'s user path plus a per-cycle budget on
+  the advisor tail; the barrier test pins both.

diff --git a/docs/how-it-works.md b/docs/how-it-works.md
index 984f030041..e25f7fa5fb 100644
--- a/docs/how-it-works.md
+++ b/docs/how-it-works.md
@@ -107,12 +107,15 @@ more expensive hours in the validation scenarios.
 
 **Several starting points, not one.** A single gradient run can stop at a
 locally optimal schedule that a different starting guess beats — that is what
-the two-zone model showed. So each space solve scores four candidate profiles
+the two-zone model showed. So each space solve scores five candidate profiles
 cheaply (a warm start or the naive guess, two price-ranked profiles at
-different total energy, and a flat half-headroom guess), refines every one of
-them with L-BFGS-B, and keeps whichever refinement scores best. Four candidates
-close most of the local-optimum gap in the two-zone model; a fifth would not be
-worth the extra full solve on the hardware Home Assistant runs on.
+different total energy, a flat half-headroom guess, and the all-off plan with
+every step at its lower bound), refines every one of them with L-BFGS-B, and
+keeps whichever refinement scores best. The all-off candidate is there because
+every other one buys energy: on a day whose cheapest plan buys none, such as
+negative prices on a storage plant, a descent from the others can stop short
+of it. Each candidate costs one full solve on the hardware Home Assistant runs
+on, so the set stays this small.
 
 ---

+# --- R11-SEAM-solver: the start set brackets the all-off and wood-covered
+# optima, the risk premium stays out of every published money figure, and a
+# slot's reason tie is ordered ------------------------------------------------
+import contextlib as _sv_ctx  # noqa: E402
+from unittest import mock as _sv_mock  # noqa: E402
+
+_sv_optmod = sys.modules[type(_rk["optimizer"]).__module__]
+
+# D1-s1-51: a 2:2 reason tie inside one slot. ``max`` over a ``set`` picks by
+# the set's iteration order, which is PYTHONHASHSEED's. For a two-code set that
+# order follows insertion when both codes land in one hash slot, and then a set
+# also returns each spelling's first code, so a fixed pair passes a ``set``
+# revert under some seeds. The pair is therefore chosen under the running seed:
+# the first pair of action codes (synthetic codes after them) whose set order
+# is the same whichever code is inserted first. For it, a ``set`` reads one
+# winner for both spellings of the tie, and the slot's first code differs
+# between them, whatever the hash seed.
+from itertools import combinations as _sv_pairs  # noqa: E402
+
+from heatpump_optimizer.const import HEAT_PUMP_ACTION_STATES as _sv_codes  # noqa: E402
+
+_sv_pair = next(
+    (a, b)
+    for a, b in _sv_pairs(
+        [c for c in _sv_codes if c != "idle"]
+        + [f"reason_{n}" for n in range(1000)], 2)
+    if list({a, b}) == list({b, a})
+)
+_sv_ts = [_G_START + timedelta(minutes=15 * i) for i in range(4)]
+_sv_ties = [
+    plan_slots(_sv_ts, [1.0] * 4, [1.0] * 4, 0.25, reasons=[x, x, y, y])
+    for x, y in (_sv_pair, _sv_pair[::-1])
+]
+R.check(
+    "a plan slot's reason tie reads the slot's first code, whatever the "
+    "hash seed (D1-s1-51)",
+    [s[0].get("reason") for s in _sv_ties] == [_sv_pair[0], _sv_pair[1]],
+    f"{_sv_pair}: {[s[0].get('reason') for s in _sv_ties]}",
+)
+
+# D2-s3-01: the premium lambda*sigma prices the objective only. The reference
+# thermostat's cost does not depend on the plan, so lambda moves it only if
+# the premium is booked as money; the published prices are the input's; the
+# plan's own cost is its draw on the input prices; and every settlement price
+# the solve hands the stored-heat booking is the input's.
+_sv_raw = np.asarray(_rk["prices"], dtype=float)
+_sv_settle_prices = []
+_sv_opt = _rk["optimizer"]
+_sv_real_def, _sv_real_gap = _sv_opt._deferred_energy_cost, _sv_opt._start_gap_cost
+
+
+def _sv_spy_def(base, opt_end, prices, *a, **kw):
+    _sv_settle_prices.append(np.array(prices, dtype=float))
+    return _sv_real_def(base, opt_end, prices, *a, **kw)
+
+
+def _sv_spy_gap(state, weather, targets, prices, *a, **kw):
+    _sv_settle_prices.append(np.array(prices, dtype=float))
+    return _sv_real_gap(state, weather, targets, prices, *a, **kw)
+
+
+_sv_opt._deferred_energy_cost, _sv_opt._start_gap_cost = _sv_spy_def, _sv_spy_gap
+try:
+    _sv_on = _rk_solve(1.0, _rk_sigma)
+finally:
+    del _sv_opt._deferred_energy_cost, _sv_opt._start_gap_cost
+_sv_zero = _rk_solve(0.0, _rk_sigma)
+_sv_n = len(_sv_on.power_schedule)
+_sv_draw = np.asarray(_sv_on.power_schedule, dtype=float) + np.asarray(

+_sv_opt.optimize(inputs=solve_inputs(

+R.check(
+    "lambda=1 books no premium as money: the published prices are the input's, "

+    np.array_equal(np.asarray(_sv_on.prices, dtype=float), _sv_raw[:_sv_n])
+    and _sv_on.baseline_cost == _sv_zero.baseline_cost
+    and abs(_sv_on.predicted_cost - _sv_paid) <= 1e-9
+    and len(_sv_settle_prices) > 0

+    f"baseline {_sv_on.baseline_cost:.4f} vs {_sv_zero.baseline_cost:.4f}, "

+    return _sv_ms_real(objective, starts, bounds, *a, **kw)

+_sv_commits = []
+_sv_commit_real = _sv_optmod._commit_runs
+
+
+def _sv_commit_spy(opt, h, scope, relaxed, *a, **kw):
+    _sv_commits.append(([np.array(r, dtype=float) for r in relaxed],
+                        np.array([b[0] for b in scope[0]], dtype=float)))
+    return _sv_commit_real(opt, h, scope, relaxed, *a, **kw)
+
+
+def _sv_starts(dhw, share=None):
+    sc = _mk_golden(hours=24, dhw=dhw)
+    _sv_calls.clear()
+    _sv_commits.clear()
+    patches = [_sv_mock.patch.object(_sv_optmod, "_multi_start_minimize", _sv_ms_spy),
+               _sv_mock.patch.object(_sv_optmod, "_commit_runs", _sv_commit_spy)]
+    if share is not None:
+        patches.append(_sv_mock.patch.object(
+            _sv_optmod, "_wood_covered_share", lambda *a, **k: share))
+    with _sv_ctx.ExitStack() as stack:
+        for p in patches:
+            stack.enter_context(p)
+        sc["optimizer"].optimize(inputs=solve_inputs(
+            initial_state=sc["state"], prices=sc["prices"], outdoor_temps=sc["outdoor"],
+            wind_speeds=sc["wind"], precipitation=sc["rain"],
+            solar_radiation=sc["solar"], start_time=_G_START,
+        ))
+    return list(_sv_calls)
+
+
+_sv_space = _sv_starts(False)
+_sv_space_commits = list(_sv_commits)
+_sv_dhw = _sv_starts(True)
+R.check(
+    "the first multi-start of each solve path starts one run at the lower "
+    "bound, the all-off plan (D0-s3-02)",
+    bool(_sv_space) and bool(_sv_dhw)
+    and all(any(np.array_equal(s, lb) for s in starts)
+            for starts, lb in (_sv_space[0], _sv_dhw[0])),
+    f"{len(_sv_space)} space-only and {len(_sv_dhw)} DHW multi-starts",
+)
+R.check(

+def scratch_clone(root: Path, dst: Path, rev: str | None = None) -> Path:
+    """`root`'s tree as it would be committed, in a plain clone at `dst`: HEAD
+    checked out, the working tree's changes and unignored new files laid over
+    it and staged, the origin refs and tags a step may name copied; with
+    `rev`, that commit's tree and nothing laid over it. A clone
+    takes no per-clone config, so no merge driver, hook path or identity the
+    recording seat's session set reaches a traced step (carry 2 of
+    R11-PRE-SHARED-FILES: a seat whose hook had installed the drivers recorded
+    a step that installs them when missing without the reads a fresh checkout
+    makes); and it is a repository of its own, where a linked worktree's index
+    and object store are two directories."""
+    def git(*args: str, cwd: Path = dst, check: bool = True) -> str:
+        return subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=check).stdout
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tests"))
+    try:
+        from throwaway_git import throwaway_git_clone   # git >= 2.54 may repack a raw clone after it is removed
+    finally:
+        sys.path.pop(0)
+    throwaway_git_clone(root, dst, "-q", "--no-checkout", cwd=root)
+    head = git("rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", f"{rev or 'HEAD'}^{{commit}}", cwd=root, check=False).strip()
+    if head:
+        git("checkout", "-q", "--detach", head)
+    git("fetch", "-q", str(root), "+refs/remotes/origin/*:refs/remotes/origin/*",
+        "+refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*", check=False)
+    url = git("config", "--get", "remote.origin.url", cwd=root, check=False).strip()
+    if url:
+        git("remote", "set-url", "origin", url)
+    listed = "" if rev else git("ls-files", "-z", "-m", "-o", "-d", "--exclude-standard", cwd=root)
+    listed += "" if rev else git("diff", "--cached", "--name-only", "-z", *([head] if head else []), cwd=root)
+    for rel in sorted({r for r in listed.split("\0") if r}):

+def touched_steps(changes: list[tuple[str, str]], table: dict | None, steps: list[Step]) -> list[str]:
+    """The gated steps whose own script a diff changes -- a changed path the
+    step's command text names -- and one the table has no entry for or records
+    under another run text. A changed file a step only loads is left to main's
+    drift step: tracing every step that recorded a changed file was 17 steps
+    and 43 minutes for one diff (R11-PRE-SHARED-FILES part 1's own), more than
+    the drift it prevents costs (dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-FAMILY-SELFTEST-SCOPE-DRIFT.md)."""
+    held = (table or {}).get("steps", {})
+    text = step_commands(steps)
+
+    def named(path: str, run: str) -> bool:
+        return re.search(rf"(?<![\w./-]){re.escape(path)}(?![\w./-])", run) is not None
+    return [s.id for s in steps if s.gated and (
+        (held.get(s.id) or {}).get("run_sha") != s.run_sha
+        or any(named(p, text[s.id]) for _, p in changes))]
+

+def base_drift(root: Path, base: str, refuse: list[str], want: list[str]) -> set[str]:
+    """The refusals of `refuse` the merge base's own tree draws too, each
+    printed as a note: main's drift step is red on them already, so they are
+    the record beat's to absorb, never a branch's to pay (the step-replay rule
+    of tools/pr/ci_predict.py: a red at both ends is not the diff's). Only the
+    refused steps are traced again, at the merge base, against its table."""
+    def git(*args: str) -> str | None:
+        r = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
+        return r.stdout if r.returncode == 0 else None
+    mb = (git("merge-base", base, "HEAD") or "").strip()
+    was = job_steps(git("show", f"{mb}:{WORKFLOW}") or "") if mb else []
+    hit = {i for i in gated_ids(was) if i in want and any(f" step {i}: " in r for r in refuse)}
+    if not hit or mb == (git("rev-parse", "HEAD") or "").strip():
+        return set()
+    print(f"selftest_scope precheck: {len(refuse)} refusal(s) at the head; tracing {sorted(hit)} "
+          f"at the merge base {mb[:12]}", flush=True)
+    measured, _, _ = trace_steps(root, was, hit, mb)
+    shared = set(drift(parse_table(git("show", f"{mb}:{TABLE}")), measured, was, hit)[0]) & set(refuse)
+    for line in sorted(shared):
+        print(f"  note: the merge base draws it too, main's to absorb: {line}")
+    return shared
+
+
+def precheck(root: Path, base: str) -> int:
+    """The drift check a pull request cannot get from CI, on the seat: 0 when
+    no touched step reads past the table, 1 naming each read it misses, 3 when
+    the steps cannot be traced here or one exits non-zero under the tracer --
+    its trace is graded as far as it ran, and whether it passes is the pull
+    request's own `instrument-self-tests` run, which runs it untraced (a
+    self-test with a time bound can fail under strace alone). A refusal the
+    merge base draws too is main's standing drift, a note (`base_drift`)."""
+    steps = workflow_steps(root)
+    changes = diff_changes(base, "HEAD", root)
+    if changes is None:
+        print(f"selftest_scope precheck: git cannot diff {base}...HEAD", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    table = load_table(root / TABLE)
+    want = touched_steps(changes, table, steps)
+    if not want:
+        print("selftest_scope precheck: the diff changes no gated step's own script")
+        return 0
+    if shutil.which("strace") is None or _traced():
+        print(f"selftest_scope precheck: skip, {len(want)} step(s) untraced {want}: no strace here, "
+              f"or this run is itself traced; main's drift step is the detector")
+        return SKIP_RC
+    measured, broken, failed = trace_steps(root, steps, set(want))
+    refuse = drift(table, measured, steps, set(want))[0]
+    shared = base_drift(root, base, refuse, want)   # one trace of the merge base for all of them
+    refuse = broken + [r for r in refuse if r not in shared]
+    for line in refuse:
+        print(f"  {line}")
+    print(f"selftest_scope precheck: {len(want)} step(s) traced {want}, {len(refuse)} refusal(s)"
+          + (f" -- add the reads with `python3 {SELF} record"
+             + "".join(f" --step {i}" for i in want) + "`" if refuse else ""))
+    if failed and not refuse:
+        print(f"selftest_scope precheck: skip, {len(failed)} step(s) {failed} exited non-zero under the "
+              f"tracer, so their reads past that point are unmeasured; main's drift step is the detector")
+    return 1 if refuse else SKIP_RC if failed else 0

+def absorb_entries(table: dict, sources: list[dict], steps: list[Step], tracked: set[str],
+                   tracked_dirs: set[str], gone: set[str]) -> tuple[dict[str, dict], list[str]]:
+    """(entries, added): the live table with every read a source table holds
+    for a step whose run text is this head's, by `union_record`; `added` names
+    each new read as `step ID: KIND ITEM`. A source is main's own measurement
+    at an older commit, so a read of it that names nothing at this head (a file
+    since deleted, a path since retired or ignored: `gone`) is not carried, and
+    a step recorded under another run text is not this step's measurement."""
+    live = {s.id: s.run_sha for s in steps if s.gated}
+
+    def here(kind: str, item: str) -> bool:
+        whole = item.endswith("/**")
+        name = item[:-3] if whole else item
+        if kind == "git":
+            return True
+        if kind == "dirs" or whole:
+            return name in tracked_dirs
+        return item in tracked if kind == "files" else probe_path(item, tracked_dirs) and item not in gone
+
+    entries = {k: v for k, v in table["steps"].items()}
+    added: list[str] = []
+    for src in sources:
+        for sid, got in sorted(src.get("steps", {}).items()):
+            if live.get(sid) != got.get("run_sha"):
+                continue
+            old = entries.get(sid) or {}
+            new = {**got, **{k: [x for x in got.get(k, ()) if here(k, x)] for k in LIST_KINDS}}
+            merged = union_record({"steps": entries}, {sid: new}, set(live))[sid]
+            added += [f"step {sid}: {k} {x}" for k in LIST_KINDS
+                      for x in merged[k] if x not in old.get(k, ())]
+            added += [f"step {sid}: {k}" for k in FLAG_KINDS if merged[k] and not old.get(k)]
+            entries[sid] = merged
+    return entries, added
+
+
+def absorb_cli(sources: list[Path], out: Path, root: Path = ROOT) -> int:
+    """Write `out` as the live table unioned with the source tables, when that
+    adds a read; print each one added (the generator's diff)."""
+    table = load_table(root / TABLE)
+    loaded = [load_table(p) for p in sources]
+    if table is None or None in loaded:
+        bad = [TABLE] * (table is None) + [str(p) for p, t in zip(sources, loaded) if t is None]
+        print(f"selftest_scope absorb: UNREADABLE {bad}, nothing written", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    tracked, tracked_dirs = _tracked(root)
+    probes = {p for t in loaded for e in t["steps"].values() for p in e.get("probes", ())}
+    retired = [r.rstrip("/") for r in retired_paths(root)]
+    gone = _ignored(root, probes) | {p for p in probes
+                                     if any(p == r or p.startswith(r + "/") for r in retired)}
+    entries, added = absorb_entries(table, loaded, workflow_steps(root), tracked, tracked_dirs, gone)
+    for line in added:
+        print(f"  + {line}")
+    if added:
+        write_table(out, entries, root)
+    print(f"selftest_scope absorb: {len(added)} read(s) added to "
+          f"{len({a.split(':')[0] for a in added})} step(s)")
+    return 0
+

+# The mutants run JOBS at a time (55 runs of a self-test that waits more than

+# and a third of the job's own timeout); each writes its report to a file of
+# its own and the reports are printed in order once all have ended. Four to a

+# to a processor still outlasted that replay on a seat slower than the one it

+SCOPE_TOOL = "tools/ci/selftest_scope.py"

+def selftest_scope_preds(root: Path, base: str, notes: list | None = None,
+                         run=subprocess.run) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+    """Main's drift step, the one `instrument-self-tests` check no pull request
+    runs (dev/audit/rca/R10-RCA-SELFTEST-SCOPE-DRIFT.md: a diff that gives a
+    gated self-test a new read turned main red after its merge, ten hotfixes in
+    round 10). `selftest_scope.py precheck` traces the gated steps whose own
+    script the diff changes, in a scratch clone, and grades them as
+    that step does: each read the table misses is a predicted red naming its
+    repair; rc 3 (no strace here) is a note, main's step staying the detector."""
+    if not (root / SCOPE_TOOL).is_file():
+        return []
+    r = run([sys.executable, "-I", SCOPE_TOOL, "precheck", "--base", base], cwd=root,
+            capture_output=True, text=True)
+    lines = [x for x in r.stdout.splitlines() if x.strip()]
+    if r.returncode == 3:
+        (notes if notes is not None else []).append("SELFTEST SCOPE " + (lines[-1] if lines else "skipped"))
+        return []
+    if r.returncode == 0:
+        return []
+    refused = [x.strip() for x in lines if x.startswith("  ")]
+    if r.returncode != 1 or not refused:
+        tail = (lines or r.stderr.splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1]
+        return [("instrument", f"SELFTEST SCOPE UNREADABLE precheck rc {r.returncode}: {tail}")]
+    out = []
+    for x in refused:
+        m = re.search(r"\bstep ([\w-]+)", x)
+        out.append(("instrument", f"SELFTEST SCOPE {x}" + (
+            f" -- `python3 {SCOPE_TOOL} record --step {m.group(1)}` adds what the step reads now" if m else "")))
+    return out
+
+

+def overlay_program(wt: str, base: str, head: str, files: list[str], exclude: str) -> dict:
+    """Lay the base's copy of ``files`` over the head's worktree ``wt``; the environment the run needs.
+
+    The overlay is the program the run executes, never the head's change, and an
+    instrument that asks git what the branch changed (`tests/closure.py`'s
+    `changed_files`: tracked changes against HEAD, then untracked files) must not
+    be handed it: a branch forked before main changed `tests/closure.py` read as
+    having edited a gate file and rendered `MODE: FULL`. The index goes back to
+    the head's; a file the head tracks is marked skip-worktree, and one only the
+    base has is named in an excludes file the returned environment points git at.
+    """
+    if not files:
+        return {}
+    for f in files:
+        _git(wt, "checkout", base, "--", f)  # the base's program, not the head's
+    _git(wt, "reset", "-q", head, "--", *files)
+    tracked = [f for f in _git(wt, "ls-files", "--", *files).split("\n") if f]
+    if tracked:
+        _git(wt, "update-index", "--skip-worktree", "--", *tracked)
+    with open(exclude, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        fh.write("".join(f"/{f}\n" for f in files if f not in tracked))
+    return {"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT": "1", "GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0": "core.excludesFile", "GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0": exclude}

+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "prog.sh"), "w").write(seen)
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "ver"), "w").write("1")
+        g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-qm", "main registers a program")
+        g("checkout", "-qb", "old")
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "f"), "w").write("3")
+        g("commit", "-qam", "a branch that touches no program")
+        g("checkout", "-q", "main")
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "ver"), "w").write("2")
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "late"), "w").write("added after the fork")
+        g("add", "-A"); g("commit", "-qm", "main changes the program and adds a file to it")
+        g("checkout", "-q", "old")
+        old_sha, old_mb = context(tmp, "main", "HEAD")
+        check("a program main changed or added after the fork runs as the base's and is not the head's diff",
+              run_instrument(tmp, "main", old_sha, old_mb, "seen", load_registry(tmp, "main")) == "ran:2")
+        open(os.path.join(tmp, "ver"), "w").write("mine")
+        g("commit", "-qam", "the branch edits the program itself")
+        own_sha, own_mb = context(tmp, "main", "HEAD")
+        check("null: a file the instrument's run leaves changed in the head's tree is still listed",
+              run_instrument(tmp, "main", own_sha, own_mb, "seen",
+                             {**load_registry(tmp, "main"), "seen": {"argv": ["sh", "-e", "-c", "echo x > f; " + seen.strip()], "files": []}})
+              == "f\nran:mine")
     finally:
         shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
     failed = results.count(False)
